states.statusText: The last UT subsidy scheme lapsed on 31 Mar 2020, and no successor has been issued.

portal.label: Directorate of Industries

states.notes: Industrial-estate plots and sheds are allotted under the 2025 allotment policy.

items.name: Industrial estate plots/sheds (A&N Industrial Estate (Allotment & Management) Policy 2025)
items.summary: Plots and sheds in Directorate of Industries estates allotted under the 2025 allotment policy; concessions unconfirmed.
details: Policy notified around March 2025 covers all existing and upcoming Directorate of Industries estates (e.g., Gharacharma, Dollygunj, Bakultala, Mithakhari, Campbell Bay, Little Andaman). Allotment rates, rent concessions and reservations unconfirmed.
conditions: Terms per 2025 policy (unconfirmed); eligible activities unconfirmed

items.name: RAMP Tourism Interventions 2026-27 (A&N Directorate of Tourism)
items.summary: Equipment subsidy for astro-tourism (telescopes etc.) and free training and certification for homestay staff; subsidy rate not confirmed
details: Two interventions notified on 5 Aug 2026: training, certification and exposure programme for homestay staff, and subsidy on purchase of astro-tourism equipment.
Selected beneficiaries buy the equipment and claim reimbursement of the subsidy.
conditions: Open to eligible MSMEs, homestay owners and staff, and individuals in the islands.
Expressions of interest were due by 20 Aug 2026 to the Planning Section, Directorate of Tourism; forms are in Gazette No. 243 of 5 Aug 2026. Watch for a further round.

states.short: AP MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29)
states.statusText: In force. All figures below come from a consultancy summary, not the official G.O.; confirm them with the DIC.

portal.label: AP Industries Department

states.zones: No location zones; rates vary with size, new unit or expansion, and special-category ownership.
states.notes: AP counts BC owners as special category, but the AP BC list differs from the central OBC list. No interest subsidy was found.

items.name: Capital subsidy (new and expansion/diversification)
items.summary: New units: 25% of fixed capital investment, capped at ₹25 lakh (micro), ₹1.5 crore (small), ₹7 crore (medium).
details: New units, general: 25% (micro ≤₹25L, small ≤₹1.5 Cr, medium ≤₹7 Cr). Expansion/diversification, general: 20% (micro ≤₹20L, small ≤₹2 Cr, medium ≤₹5 Cr). SC/ST transport services: 45%, caps ₹45L (micro) and ₹75L (small/medium).
items.extraFor: Special category (100% owned by women, SC, ST, BC, minority, specially-abled or transgender entrepreneurs; AP domicile): new units 45% (micro ≤₹45L, small ≤₹4.5 Cr), medium 35% ≤₹7 Cr; expansion 40% (≤₹40L, ≤₹4 Cr), medium 30% ≤₹5 Cr
conditions: Minimum expansion size unconfirmed

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of net SGST reimbursed for 5 years, capped at 5% of annual turnover.

items.name: Power subsidy
items.summary: ₹1 per unit for 5 years (₹1.50 for special category); annual cap ₹1 lakh micro, ₹5 lakh small/medium.
items.extraFor: Special category: ₹1.50/unit
conditions: Manufacturing or eligible service activities

items.name: Stamp duty reimbursement
items.summary: 100% stamp duty reimbursement.

items.name: Land conversion reimbursement and SC/ST land rebate
items.summary: 100% land conversion (CLU) charge reimbursement; SC/ST land cost rebate of 75% up to ₹25 lakh.
details: The SC/ST rebate covers land cost only, for new micro/small units wholly owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs.
items.extraFor: SC/ST: 75% land rebate ≤₹25L
conditions: AP domicile for the SC/ST rebate

items.name: Skill upgradation / EPF support
items.summary: ₹5,000 per trainee (micro, max 10), ₹10,000 (small, max 20); medium: employer EPF up to ₹1 lakh a year.
details: Medium: 100% of employer EPF contribution, capped at ₹1 lakh a year, for 3 years.

items.name: Water and energy audits
items.summary: 75% of water audit (≤₹1 lakh) and energy audit (≤₹2 lakh) cost; 25% of recommended equipment.
details: Equipment cap: ₹20L (micro), ₹40L (small), ₹50L (medium).

items.name: Local-procurement incentive for exporters
items.summary: 1% of annual export turnover for 3 years; overall cap ₹15 lakh (micro), ₹1.5 crore (small), ₹7 crore (medium).

items.name: SC/ST transport service enterprises capital subsidy (MEDP 4.0 amendment, G.O.Ms.No.22, 2025)
items.summary: SC/ST transport service units: 45% capital subsidy (micro up to ₹45 lakh, small up to ₹75 lakh); medium 35% up to ₹75 lakh
details: Added by G.O.Ms.No.22 (17 Feb 2025) under the 'One Family, One Entrepreneur by 2030' goal, because SC/ST entrepreneurs often run transport businesses.
Micro: 45% of fixed capital investment up to ₹45 lakh; small: 45% up to ₹75 lakh; medium: 35% up to ₹75 lakh; each paid in 2 instalments.
conditions: Enterprise wholly owned by SC or ST entrepreneurs domiciled in Andhra Pradesh; policy period 26 Oct 2024 to 25 Oct 2029.
Claim online on the AP MSME ONE portal within 6 months of start of commercial operation (50% if filed in 6-12 months).
items.onlyText: Only for transport service enterprises wholly owned by SC or ST entrepreneurs

items.name: AP Neighbourhood Workspace Policy 2025-30 (incentives for workspace developers)
items.summary: Neighbourhood workspace developers: 60% interiors subsidy up to ₹15 lakh, 50% IT hardware up to ₹5 lakh, rent and 8% interest support
details: Interior development: 60% up to ₹15 lakh for the first approved workspace in a mandal, 50% up to ₹7.5 lakh for later ones; IT hardware 50% up to ₹5 lakh (one-time).
Rent: 100% exemption for 5 years in government buildings (first per mandal) or 50% up to ₹6 lakh a year in private buildings; broadband 50% up to ₹1 lakh a year for 5 years.
Interest subsidy of 8% a year, up to ₹10,000 a month for 5 years, on loans for interiors and IT hardware.
conditions: Workspace of at least 1,000 sq ft with 10 workstations, meeting room with VC, 24x7 power backup, CCTV and other listed facilities.
Issued by G.O.Ms.No.52 (IT, E&C Dept, 11 Nov 2025); apply to the IT department once operating guidelines are notified.
apply: AP IT, Electronics and Communications Department

items.name: AP Innovation and Startup Policy 4.0 (2024-29) - startup grants and incentives
items.summary: Startup grant up to Rs 15 lakh (Rs 20 lakh for women, SC, ST, BC, minority or disabled founders), plus 8% interest subsidy and 100% net SGST for 5 years
details: Grants are released in three phases (15% or Rs 2 lakh, then 30%, then 55%).
Seed and go-to-market funding up to Rs 50 lakh each on an equity-sharing basis; deep-tech seed funding up to Rs 1 crore.
Interest subsidy of 8% on term loans; 75% of event participation cost up to Rs 3 lakh; 50% of accelerator fees up to Rs 2 lakh; 50% of patent costs up to Rs 2 lakh (India) or Rs 10 lakh (foreign).
Policy notified by G.O.Ms.No.3 dated 24 Mar 2025; operating guidelines G.O.Ms.No.9 dated 28 Apr 2025.
items.extraFor: Grant up to Rs 20 lakh for startups 100% owned by women, SC, ST, BC, minority or differently abled entrepreneurs
conditions: Private limited company, registered partnership or LLP registered in Andhra Pradesh, up to 10 years old, turnover never above Rs 100 crore.
Project approval by Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS); interest and SGST claims within 6 months of commercial operations.
items.onlyText: Only for innovative startups up to 10 years old registered in Andhra Pradesh

items.name: AP Textile, Apparel and Garments Policy 4.0 (2024-29): investment subsidy
items.summary: 30% of eligible fixed capital investment for new textile/apparel MSMEs (cap Rs 3 cr micro/small, Rs 10 cr medium); 45% for special categories
details: Micro and small: 30% of eFCI, capped at Rs 3 crore; medium: 30%, capped at Rs 10 crore.
Value-added activities: 40% of eFCI, capped at Rs 20 crore (55% for special categories).
100% reimbursement of stamp and transfer duty on industrial land, leases and mortgages.
Skill upgradation: Rs 5,000 per person (micro, up to 10) or Rs 10,000 per person (small, up to 20); medium units get employer EPF reimbursement up to Rs 1 lakh a year for 3 years.
Policy runs 11 Dec 2024 to 10 Dec 2029 (G.O.Ms.No.89, 11 Dec 2024; operational guidelines 10 Apr 2025).
items.extraFor: Additional 15% of eFCI (total 45%) for enterprises of women, BC, SC, ST, minority, specially abled or transgender entrepreneurs domiciled in AP; 75% land-cost rebate up to Rs 25 lakh for SC/ST.
conditions: Textile, apparel and garment manufacturing units in Andhra Pradesh.
File the claim within 6 months of commercial production (50% if filed 6-12 months late); stay in production 6 years (MSE) or 8 years (medium).
Total incentives capped at 75% of fixed capital investment.
Apply online under Apply for Industrial Incentives on apindustries.gov.in.

items.name: AP Textile, Apparel and Garments Policy 4.0: technology upgradation subsidy for existing units
items.summary: 30% of eligible investment for existing textile MSMEs that expand or modernise (cap Rs 2 cr micro/small, Rs 7.5 cr medium); 45% for special categories
details: For existing MSMEs undertaking expansion, diversification or modernisation, not new units.
Micro and small: 30%, capped at Rs 2 crore; medium: 30%, capped at Rs 7.5 crore.
items.extraFor: 45% (additional 15%) for women, BC, SC, ST, minority, specially abled or transgender entrepreneurs.
conditions: Existing textile, apparel or garment unit in Andhra Pradesh.
Micro and small claims go to the District Industries and Export Promotion Committee; medium to the State Level Committee.
Apply on apindustries.gov.in.

items.name: AP Textile, Apparel and Garments Policy 4.0: power cost subsidy and electricity duty
items.summary: Rs 2 per unit power subsidy for 5 years (cap Rs 2 lakh/yr micro, Rs 10 lakh small, Rs 30 lakh medium) plus 50% electricity duty exemption
details: Power cost: Rs 2 per unit for five years from commercial production; annual caps Rs 2 lakh (micro), Rs 10 lakh (small), Rs 30 lakh (medium), as revised by G.O.Ms.No.24 of 17 Feb 2025.
Electricity duty: 50% exemption for five years from commercial production.
conditions: New textile, apparel or garment MSME in Andhra Pradesh.
Apply on apindustries.gov.in.

items.name: AP Food Processing Policy 4.0 (2024-29): capital subsidy for food processing MSMEs
items.summary: Capital subsidy of 25% (primary) to 35% (secondary/tertiary processing) of fixed capital; reported caps Rs 35 lakh micro, Rs 3.5 cr small, Rs 8 cr medium
details: Reported rates: primary processing 25% of FCI (caps Rs 25 lakh micro, Rs 1.5 crore small, Rs 7 crore medium); secondary/tertiary processing 35% (caps Rs 35 lakh, Rs 3.5 crore, Rs 8 crore).

Also reported: 100% net SGST reimbursement for 6 years (up to 5% of turnover), power tariff reimbursement of Rs 1 per unit, reimbursement of food-safety certification (HACCP, GMP, ISO) and stamp duty.
Figures are from secondary summaries; confirm in the policy before applying.
items.extraFor: Reported additional 10% for units wholly owned by women, BC, SC, ST, minority, specially abled or transgender entrepreneurs.
conditions: Food processing manufacturing units in Andhra Pradesh.
Apply through the AP Single Desk / industries portal; the Food Processing Society of AP is the nodal agency.

items.onlyText: Only for Backward Class and Economically Weaker Section applicants from BPL families
items.name: AP BC and EWS Corporation self-employment subsidy units (OBMMS)
items.summary: Subsidy-linked bank loans for BC and EWS units; FY 2024-25 outlay ₹1,280 crore, no beneficiary contribution
details: January 2025 guidelines: ₹896 crore for 1.3 lakh BC beneficiaries and ₹384 crore for 59,000 EWS beneficiaries; government subsidy covers part of the unit cost and banks lend the rest.
Units include mini dairies, sheep and goat units, carpentry, traditional crafts and generic medicine stores. Subsidy share for 2025-26 not confirmed.
conditions: BC or EWS applicant from a BPL family, aged 21 to 60.
Apply through the village or ward secretariat or online on the OBMMS portal.

items.name: Free power to handloom weaver households and powerloom units (G.O.Ms.No.44, 2025)
items.summary: Free electricity up to 200 units/month for handloom weavers and up to 500 units/month for powerloom units
details: Ordered by G.O.Ms.No.44, Industries and Commerce Department, 26 March 2025; in force from 1 April 2026.
Consumption above the free units is billed at normal DISCOM rates; about 93,000 handloom and 11,488 powerloom families covered.
conditions: Handloom weaver households and powerloom units in Andhra Pradesh, as per the department SoP.
Enrolment through the Handlooms and Textiles Department and DISCOM; contact the Assistant Director (Handlooms) of the district.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom weaver households and powerloom units

items.name: AP Tourism Policy 2024-29: SGST, stamp duty and land conversion relief for tourism units
items.summary: Up to 100% SGST reimbursement for up to 15 years, 100% stamp duty reimbursement and 100% land conversion charge waiver
details: Tourism and hospitality have industry status, so industrial concessions apply.
Up to 100% SGST reimbursement for up to 15 years (rate and period depend on project category).
100% stamp duty reimbursement and 100% waiver of land conversion charges; capital subsidies also offered (rates not confirmed).
conditions: For new tourism projects approved by the AP Tourism Department during 2024-29
Apply through AP Tourism Authority / single window

items.name: Andhra Pradesh public procurement relaxations for startups
items.summary: EMD, turnover and experience exemption and full tender-fee waiver for startups in tenders up to Rs 50 lakh
details: Exemption from EMD, prior turnover and prior experience for eligible startups in state procurement up to Rs 50 lakh.
Full waiver of tender document cost for the same procurements.
AP-based IT startups: 100% government procurement for IT projects up to Rs 1 crore and a 5% technical evaluation advantage in larger projects.
conditions: Eligible startup recognised by the state and based in Andhra Pradesh.
Claim the exemption in tenders of AP departments and PSUs.

states.short: Arunachal Pradesh Industrial Development and Investment Policy 2025
states.statusText: In force.

portal.label: Department of Industries; apply at the District Industries Centre

states.zones: Rates are statewide; amounts depend on the investment size, priority-sector status and the share of APST staff.
states.notes: New manufacturing units, listed service units and existing units doing a substantial expansion qualify; trading does not. Units must employ at least 20% APST managers and 30% APST other staff within 3 years.

items.name: Capital Investment Incentive
items.summary: 50% of plant & machinery or service building cost; max ₹15 lakh or ₹30 lakh depending on investment.
details: Investment ₹5-25 lakh: 50%, max ₹15 lakh
Investment above ₹25 lakh up to ₹50 lakh: 50%, max ₹30 lakh
+10% of the subsidy for Priority Sectors and +10% if at least 50% (or 5) of skilled staff are APST, within the same caps
No slab is defined above ₹50 lakh
items.extraFor: Top-up linked to APST workforce share, not to owner category
conditions: New units or substantial expansion (at least 25% more investment)
Slabs stop at ₹50 lakh of eligible investment, so in practice only micro units fit
Newly purchased assets at arm's length; no relocated or refurbished machinery
Apply within 1 year of commercial production

items.name: Capital Interest Subvention (term loan)
items.summary: 5-8% interest subvention on term loans for 5 years, capped at ₹10-25 lakh.
details: Investment ₹5-25 lakh: 6% a year (Priority Sector 8%), max ₹10 lakh (₹15 lakh)
Investment above ₹25 lakh: 5% (Priority 6%), max ₹20 lakh (₹25 lakh)
Unit must bear at least 2% interest; computed on the disbursed amount
conditions: Loans from scheduled banks or RBI-registered institutions for new plant & machinery
New units or substantial expansion
Claim within 6 months after each financial year

items.name: Working Capital Interest Subvention
items.summary: 5% interest subvention on working capital loans for 5 years, up to ₹50 lakh.
details: 5% a year for 5 consecutive years; max ₹50 lakh and not above 100% of eligible investment; unit bears at least 1% interest
conditions: GST-registered units
New units or substantial expansion

items.name: Power subsidy (MSME manufacturing)
items.summary: ₹2 per unit consumed for 5 years, max ₹75 lakh a year, for MSME manufacturing units.
details: ₹2.00 per unit from commercial production for 5 years; max ₹75 lakh a year and not above 100% of plant & machinery investment; deducted in power bills
conditions: Only units on 11 kV/33 kV connections
New units or substantial expansion

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of net SGST for 7 years, capped at 250%, 200% or 180% of investment by size.
details: Micro: cap 250% of eligible investment
Small: 200%
Medium and large: 180%
7 years from commercial production; net SGST = SGST paid minus input tax credit, CA-certified
conditions: Unit must keep producing for the next 5 years at 70% or more of its average output
New units or substantial expansion

items.name: Stamp duty and registration fee reimbursement
items.summary: 100% reimbursement of stamp duty and registration fee on the land conveyance or lease deed.
details: 100% reimbursement, paid after commercial production or operation starts
conditions: Only for land allotted in Government industrial estates, parks or growth centres
Land must be specified in the DPR
New units only

items.name: Quality certification and testing facilities
items.summary: 35% of testing-equipment or certification cost, up to ₹5 lakh.
details: Covers GMP, ISO, BIS, FPO, BEE, AGMARK, ECOMARK, ZED, GHP, GRIHA, LEED and in-house testing equipment
conditions: Open to new and existing units

items.name: Air-freight transport or export subsidy
items.summary: 50% of air freight or 60% of transport to an international port, up to ₹5 lakh a year.
details: Air freight of finished goods out of the state: 50%, max ₹5 lakh a year for 5 years
Export: 60% of transport cost to the international port, max ₹5 lakh a year for 5 years
Only one of the two
conditions: Open to new and existing units
Export subsidy for registered exporters only

items.name: Green energy and pollution-control subsidies
items.summary: 50% of renewable energy system cost (10-2,000 kW), up to ₹25 lakh.
details: Solar, wind, water, biomass or hybrid systems of 10-2,000 kW: 50%, max ₹25 lakh, paid in 3 tranches over 2 years
Wastewater recycling equipment: 50%, max ₹2 lakh
Pollution-control devices (existing units): 50%, max ₹10 lakh
conditions: Open to new and existing units

items.name: Common Facility Centre usage reimbursement
items.summary: 50% of charges for using a recognised Common Facility Centre, up to ₹1 lakh a year for 3 years.
details: For handicraft, handloom, agro and food processing, and aromatic/medicinal plant units; cooperatives and FPOs also eligible
conditions: Open to new and existing units

items.name: Special incentives for underprivileged sections
items.summary: 95% of DPR consultancy fee (up to ₹1 lakh) and 10% plot reservation for eligible women and PwD.
details: 95% reimbursement of the fee for preparing the Detailed Project Report, max ₹1 lakh
10% of plots in industrial estates reserved
items.extraFor: Only women who are single mothers or widows, and persons with at least 40% disability; no SC/ST-specific provision
conditions: A woman-owned unit qualifies only if the owner is a single mother or widow
items.onlyText: Only for women owners who are single mothers or widows, and owners with at least 40% disability

items.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swavalamban Yojana (DDUSY)
items.summary: 40% front-ended capital subsidy on bank-financed projects of ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh (land and building excluded)
details: State self-employment scheme of the Finance, Planning & Investment Department; District Level Screening Committees shortlist, banks sanction loans.
Loan covers 30 to 50% of project cost and the entrepreneur puts in 10 to 30%; subsidy is credited to the loan account soon after sanction.
Sectors: food processing and cold chain, eco-tourism (homestays, tour operators), traditional weaving, small manufacturing, bamboo processing, service and diagnostic units; plantations excluded.
Online applications via the DDUSY portal (DDUSY 2025 form).
items.extraFor: Women entrepreneurs get an extra 5% annual interest subsidy while the loan stays standard
conditions: Unemployed APST youth aged 18 to 45 with at least Class XII
Submit online form with concept note, ST certificate and Aadhaar; present to the District Level Screening Committee
State gives no guarantee for loan default; loans usually covered under CGTMSE
items.onlyText: Only for unemployed Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribe (APST) youth aged 18 to 45

items.name: Arunachal Pradesh Startup Policy (2022-23)
items.summary: Proof-of-concept grants up to ₹20 lakh, scale-up grants up to ₹50 lakh, 50% R&D capex up to ₹5 lakh
details: Run by the Finance, Planning & Investment Department (Investment Division) with APIIP, the state incubator.
Patent cost reimbursement up to ₹10,000 per Indian and ₹1 lakh per international patent.
At least 20% purchase preference in state procurement, plus government trial orders.
items.extraFor: At least 33% of the Arunachal Pradesh Seed Fund is reserved for women-led startups
conditions: Startup based in Arunachal Pradesh; priority sectors include agri-horticulture, forest and bamboo, minerals and tourism
Apply through the Arunachal startup portal / APIIP
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised under the Arunachal Pradesh Startup Policy

items.name: Chief Minister's Paryatan Vikas Yojana (CMPVY)
items.summary: Rs 5 lakh direct loan subsidy for patisseries, plus support for homestay room upgrades and adventure tourism equipment
details: Patisserie and food-court component: direct loan subsidy of Rs 5 lakh.
Homestay component: support to upgrade two furnished rooms with attached toilets (shower, geyser, western toilet).
Adventure tourism component: support to buy rafts, kayaks, quad bikes and similar equipment. Amounts for homestay and adventure components not confirmed.
conditions: Arunachal Pradesh domicile.
Homestays must be registered with the Department of Tourism (trained operators get priority); patisserie and food-court operators must be registered with the Department.
Apply offline at the District Tourism Office; District Tourism Officer verifies and interviews applicants.
apply: Scheme page (District Tourism Office applies offline)

states.short: Industrial and Investment Policy of Assam 2019
states.period: From 1 Sep 2019; extended until further notice
states.statusText: In force; extended from 1 Sep 2024 until further notice.

portal.label: Assam EoDB single window; claims through the District Industries and Commerce Centre

states.zones: Rates are statewide; units in notified special parks get a higher SGST ceiling.
states.notes: Only new units that started production on or after 1 Sep 2019 qualify; expansion and trading are not covered, and services only in a few sectors. There is no capital or term-loan interest subsidy. On 24 Sep 2026 the Cabinet approved a State Capital Investment Subsidy for manufacturing units that qualify under UNNATI 2024 but could not register by its extended deadline of 30 Sep 2026; rates are not yet published.

items.name: SGST reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of SGST paid in cash for 15 years, capped at 150-250% of fixed capital investment.
details: Cap as % of fixed capital investment (FCI): micro 200% (250% inside Special Parks); small 150% (180% in parks); medium 150% (150% in parks)
Reimburses SGST paid through the electronic cash ledger for 15 years from commercial production
conditions: New units that started commercial production on or after 1 Sep 2019; no expansion provision
Must keep production at 75% or more of the preceding 5-year average, or refund
Services limited to 3-star+ hotels/resorts, river cruises and green-energy power generation

items.name: Power subsidy and generating-set subsidy
items.summary: ₹2/unit consumed for 5 years (max ₹50 lakh/year); generating sets 50% up to ₹20 lakh.
details: ₹2.00 per unit on APDCL supply for 5 years from commercial production; max ₹50 lakh per year and total not above 100% of plant & machinery investment
Generating set: 50% of cost (set, taxes, transport) up to ₹20 lakh; capacity must match sanctioned load
conditions: APDCL connections only (not open access or captive generation)
New units only

items.name: Stamp duty reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of stamp duty reimbursed, up to ₹25 lakh.
details: 100% reimbursement, ceiling ₹25 lakh, only for land used exclusively for the factory or hotel
conditions: Not available for agricultural land
Not available for land used for manufacturing in urban areas
New units only

items.name: Interest subsidy on working capital loan
items.summary: 2% interest subsidy on outstanding working capital loans for 5 years, up to ₹50 lakh.
details: 2% a year on outstanding working capital loan from banks/financial institutions for 5 years; ceiling ₹50 lakh and not above 100% of plant & machinery investment
IIPA 2019 has no term-loan interest subsidy and no capital investment subsidy
conditions: New units only
Loans from banks or financial institutions only

items.name: Technology transfer and quality certification subsidy
items.summary: 75% of quality-certification or technology-transfer fees, up to ₹10 lakh per unit.
details: 75% of fees for BIS/ISO/FSSAI-type certification or technical know-how from recognised institutions; ceiling ₹10 lakh per unit
conditions: New units only

items.name: Employment generation incentive
items.summary: One-time ₹10,000 to the employer for each local youth employed.
details: ₹10,000 per local youth employed, paid once
conditions: General condition for all IIPA incentives: at least 80% people of Assam in managerial and 90% in non-managerial posts
'Local youth' is not further defined in the policy

items.name: Effluent treatment plant subsidy
items.summary: 50% of the capital cost of an effluent treatment plant, up to ₹25 lakh.
details: 50% of ETP capital cost, ceiling ₹25 lakh per unit; not available to hotels
conditions: New units only

items.name: Assistance for MSMEs listing on a stock exchange
items.summary: 30% of public-issue expenses, up to ₹5 lakh, for MSMEs listing on BSE/NSE.
details: 30% of public issue expenses, ceiling ₹5 lakh
conditions: MSME listed on BSE or NSE
items.scope: Only once you list on the BSE or NSE SME platform

items.name: Chief Minister's Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan (CMAAA)
items.summary: ₹2 lakh (₹5 lakh for professionals) for youth enterprises: half grant, half interest-free loan
details: ₹2 lakh for matric pass, graduates, ITI and diploma holders; ₹5 lakh for professional degree holders (engineering, medical, veterinary, agriculture, etc.). Half is a grant and half an interest-free government loan.
Phases 1.0 and 2.0 under way: on 17 Sep 2026 the CM disbursed further instalments to 82,219 entrepreneurs; a third phase (CMAAA 3.0) has been reported open for registration.
conditions: Permanent resident of Assam, registered with the Employment Exchange, no loan default, one beneficiary per household (CMAAA 2.0 age limit 28 to 45 as on 1 Apr 2024).
Apply online on the CMAAA portal (small application fee).
items.onlyText: Only for Assam youth registered with the Employment Exchange (age limits apply)

items.name: Mukhya Mantri Mahila Udyamita Abhiyan (MMUA)
items.summary: Seed capital of Rs 10,000 for SHG women, then Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000 after review of use (up to Rs 85,000 in all)
details: Paid in three stages; each later stage follows a review (about six months) of how the earlier amount was used.
Cheques distributed at constituency-level events from 2025.
conditions: Women members of self-help groups in Assam.
Later instalments only for beneficiaries with up to three children.
Enrolment through the SHG and the state rural livelihoods mission network.
items.onlyText: Only for women members of self-help groups in Assam

items.name: Assam Start-up and Innovation Policy 2025 - MASI startup grants
items.summary: Grant up to Rs 10 lakh for idea to proof of concept, up to Rs 25 lakh for pilots and up to Rs 50 lakh for scale-up, plus 100% patent cost reimbursement
details: Notified February 2025; run by the Department of Innovation, Incubation and Start-ups (Assam Startup - The Nest).
Pilot grant covers MVP, equipment and certification costs; scale-up grant covers commercialisation.
Recognised startups can also seek equity from the Assam Startup SIDBI Venture Capital Fund.
conditions: Startup must hold My Assam Startup ID (MASI) recognition.
Apply on the Assam Startup portal during grant calls.
items.onlyText: Only for startups with My Assam Startup ID (MASI)

items.name: Assam Procurement Preference Policy 2021
items.summary: Local MSEs within 20% of L1 get 25% of the order; 25% annual purchase target; startups get free tender sets and 50% EMD waiver
details: Notified 6 Dec 2021 (No. MI.64/2020/25), replacing the 2015 policy.
The local MSE or startup quoting closest to L1 gets a supply order for 25% of the quantity, if within a 20% margin of L1.
Departments target 25% of annual purchases from local MSEs.
Assam startups (MASI ID) get free tender sets, 50% EMD exemption and 50% security deposit waiver.
Purchases under Rs 5 lakh and externally aided projects are excluded.
items.extraFor: ASIDC runs dedicated outreach for SC, ST and women-owned MSEs.
conditions: MSE with production base and head office in Assam, Udyam registration, at least 90% local employees and the notified local content.
Declaration of no blacklisting; preference must be stated in the tender notice.
ASIDC is the nodal agency for vendor development.

items.name: BIPONI trade fair participation scheme (Assam)
items.summary: Stall rent (up to ₹5,000 in-state; 50% up to ₹10,000 national; free stall abroad) plus travel and daily allowance
details: Fairs in Assam: stall rent up to ₹5,000 per entrepreneur paid to the organiser, plus ₹500 a day for participants from other districts.
National fairs: 50% of stall rent up to ₹10,000, sleeper-class rail fare for two persons and ₹300 per person per day.
International fairs: free shared stall space, economy air fare for one person and ₹1,000 per day; limited to 'Brand Assam' product basket units.
conditions: Micro and small enterprises in Assam.
Apply on Form A to the General Manager, District Industries and Commerce Centre when applications are advertised, with the organiser's stall-rent quotation.
apply: District Industries and Commerce Centre, Assam

items.name: Assam Logistics and Warehousing Policy 2022 - capital subsidy for warehouses, cold storage and processing centres
items.summary: 30% capital subsidy: warehouses up to ₹7.5 crore, cold storage ₹3 crore, primary processing centres ₹75 lakh, reefer vans ₹10 lakh
details: Capital subsidy of 30% of fixed capital investment: warehouses (cap ₹7.5 crore), cold storage (₹3 crore), primary processing centres (₹75 lakh), logistics parks (₹10 crore); 25% for multi-modal logistics parks (₹20 crore).
30% of the cost of refrigerated vehicles, up to ₹10 lakh.
100% stamp duty reimbursement on non-agricultural land; logistics start-ups up to ₹50 lakh; training support for women up to ₹7.5 lakh per unit.
conditions: Policy in force from 20 Aug 2022 for five years; subsidy given first come, first served within unit targets.
Bank or FI loan of at least 50% of project cost needed; warehouses and logistics parks in Kamrup Metro are not eligible for capital subsidy.
Pre-register on the EoDB single window portal before commercial operation; claim within one year of starting operations.

items.name: Amar Alohi homestay cluster scheme (Assam Tourism)
items.summary: Capital subsidy of 90% of project cost, up to Rs 1 crore, for clusters of 10+ community homestays near tourist spots
details: Supports building new homestay units and local tourism infrastructure in a cluster.
First sanction letters were issued to five community clusters (societies, SHGs, foundations) in March 2024.
conditions: Only groups or clusters with at least 10 homestay units located near tourist attractions.
Contact the Assam Tourism Department or Assam Tourism Development Corporation for the application call.
items.onlyText: Only for community groups or clusters with at least 10 homestay units

items.name: Assam Tea Industries Special Incentive Scheme (ATISIS)
items.summary: 3% interest subvention on working capital (up to Rs 20 lakh a year), orthodox/specialty tea subsidy per kg, 25% capital subsidy on machinery
details: Interest subvention of 3% a year on working capital loans, capped at Rs 20 lakh per unit per year.
Production subsidy for orthodox and specialty tea (Rs 10 per kg, reported raised to Rs 15 per kg).
Capital subsidy of 25% on plant and machinery for orthodox and specialty tea units; Rs 94.7 crore paid to 486 gardens in 2025-26.
conditions: Tea gardens and tea manufacturing units in Assam.
Apply through the Industries and Commerce or Finance Department, Assam.

items.name: Assam Cess Utilisation Policy for Small Tea Growers (special assistance to small tea factories)
items.summary: 30% of investment, up to Rs 10 lakh, for small orthodox bought-leaf or small CTC tea factories; 75% leaf-transport vehicle subsidy for STG groups
details: Small orthodox bought-leaf factory or small CTC factory: 30% of plant, machinery and building cost, up to Rs 10 lakh.
Green-leaf transport vehicle: 75% of cost, up to Rs 2 lakh (group of 5+) or Rs 3.5 lakh (10+ members).
Green-leaf collection centres: 50% to 75% of cost, up to Rs 5 lakh; 50% interest subsidy on bank loans up to Rs 10,000 per quarter.
conditions: For small tea growers, their SHGs or partnerships, and small tea factories in Assam.
Apply to the Director of Tea, Assam; valid until the state notifies otherwise (in force since 1 Jun 2015).

items.name: Swanirbhar Naari (Assam govt direct purchase of hand-woven items)
items.summary: State buys benchmarked traditional hand-woven items directly from registered weavers, without middlemen
details: Run by the Directorate of Handloom and Textiles; procurement centres in all districts.
By January 2026 Rs 19.24 crore paid for 5.55 lakh items from 19,845 weavers; 5.65 lakh applications approved.
conditions: Indigenous women weavers in Assam who weave the benchmarked items; field verification by department officers.
Register on the Swanirbhar Naari portal.
items.onlyText: Only for indigenous (mainly women) handloom weavers of Assam

states.period: Extended to 31 Dec 2026, or until the 2026 policy starts if earlier
states.statusText: Extended by the state Cabinet in Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2026, or until the new Industrial Investment Promotion Policy 2026 takes effect, whichever is earlier.

portal.label: Bihar Single Window (SWC 2.0)

source.label: Department of Industries, Bihar on X, 3 Jul 2026 (extension)

states.zones: Region A (32 less-developed districts) and Region B (Patna, Gaya, Muzaffarpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Vaishali).
states.notes: All BIIPP-2025 rates come from secondary sources.

items.name: Interest subvention (Option 1)
items.summary: Interest subvention of 12% (micro/small) or 10% a year on term loans for five years.
details: Cap as share of approved project cost: high-priority 50% (max ₹40 crore), priority 30% (max ₹20 crore), non-priority 15% (max ₹20 crore). Micro/small also get CGTMSE fee reimbursement. Mutually exclusive with the SGST-package and capital-subsidy options.
items.extraFor: SC/ST, EBC, women, differently-abled, war widows, acid-attack victims, third gender: 15% higher subvention rate and limit (secondary source)
conditions: Project cost above ₹50 lakh
New unit, or expansion after notification
Valid to 31 Dec 2026, or until the 2026 policy takes effect if earlier

items.name: SGST reimbursement (with Option 1)
items.summary: SGST reimbursed 100% (high-priority sectors) or 80% (other sectors) for five years.
details: High-priority: 100% for 5 years, capped at 100% of project cost; priority: 80%, cap 100%; non-priority: 80%, cap 70%. Projects of ₹50 crore+ may instead take a 10-14-year SGST package worth 125-300% of project cost.
conditions: Taken together with Option 1 interest subvention
Valid to 31 Dec 2026, or until the 2026 policy takes effect if earlier

items.name: Capital subsidy (Option 3, large projects)
items.summary: Capital subsidy up to 30% of approved project cost, only for projects of ₹50 crore and above.
details: Projects ₹50-200 crore: high-priority 30% (cap ₹40 crore Region A, ₹30 crore Region B), priority 25% (₹30/25 crore), non-priority 20% (₹25/20 crore); paid in equal annual instalments subject to production conditions.
conditions: Project cost ₹50 crore or more
Alternative to Options 1 and 2

items.name: Employment generation incentive
items.summary: Employer ESI/EPF reimbursed for Bihar-domiciled staff, up to ₹2,000 per employee a month for five years.
details: 100% of employer ESI/EPF contribution for Bihar-domiciled employees, max ₹2,000 per employee per month, 5 years. Reports cite ₹5,000/month for eligible labour-intensive industries and a ₹20,000-per-employee skilling grant (unconfirmed).
conditions: Bihar-domiciled employees only

items.name: BIADA land concession
items.summary: Industrial land at 50% of BIADA rate; free (₹1 token) land only for ₹100 crore+ projects.
details: ₹1 token land up to 10 acres needs over ₹100 crore investment and 1,000+ direct jobs (25 acres above ₹1,000 crore). Other investors: 50% of BIADA notified rate. At least 25% construction by 31-Mar-2027 or the full lease rate applies.
conditions: BIADA industrial area allotment

items.name: Stamp duty, registration and land-conversion fee reimbursement
items.summary: Reimbursement of stamp duty, registration and land-conversion fees; percentages unconfirmed.
details: Listed as package components by All India Radio; rates and caps not confirmed.
conditions: Valid to 31 Dec 2026, or until the 2026 policy takes effect if earlier

items.name: Quality certification, patent and green support
items.summary: Quality certification 50% up to ₹2 lakh; patent 50% up to ₹2 lakh (₹6 lakh foreign).
details: Quality certification: 50%, max ₹2 lakh for MSMEs. Patent: 50% of filing/attorney cost, max ₹2 lakh domestic, ₹6 lakh foreign. Also effluent treatment (ETP/ZLD/STP) 25% up to ₹1 crore for priority sectors; rooftop renewable (above 10 kW) 20% up to ₹6 lakh.
conditions: Valid to 31 Dec 2026, or until the 2026 policy takes effect if earlier

items.name: Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana (MMUY)
items.summary: Up to ₹10 lakh assistance to start new micro units; beneficiaries chosen by lottery.
details: Grant/interest-free-loan split and category list not confirmed from official text. 2025-26 round: applications 25-Feb to 23-Mar-2026; randomised selection 20-May-2026. Next round unconfirmed.
items.extraFor: Reported target groups: SC/ST, EBC, women, youth, minority (unconfirmed)
conditions: Pre-establishment scheme for new enterprises; an already-running Udyam unit is unlikely to qualify
Annual application window on udyami.bihar.gov.in
items.onlyText: For SC/ST, EBC, women, young and minority entrepreneurs

items.name: Bihar Laghu Udyami Yojana (BLUY)
items.summary: Grant of up to ₹2 lakh, paid in instalments, for poor families to start a small business
details: Grant (not a loan) of up to ₹2 lakh per family for self-employment, released in instalments after training; a second instalment of ₹1 lakh was paid to earlier beneficiaries in Dec 2024.
Run by the Department of Industries, Bihar, on the udyami.bihar.gov.in portal alongside the Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana.
conditions: Bihar resident aged 18 or more; family monthly income of ₹6,000 or less (families identified in the Bihar caste-based socio-economic survey); one member per family.
Mandatory short training; beneficiaries must buy the project toolkit and upload utilisation certificates.
Applications open only in notified windows (the 2024-25 window ran 19 Feb to 5 Mar 2025); check the portal for the next round.
items.onlyText: Only for poor families with monthly income of ₹6,000 or less

items.name: Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana
items.summary: ₹10,000 first grant to one woman per family to start a business, with further support up to ₹2 lakh after review
details: First instalment of ₹10,000 by direct benefit transfer to start an employment venture; payments began in September 2025.
The Bihar cabinet approved a second instalment, scheduled from February 2026.
Further assistance of up to ₹2 lakh, based on assessment of the business and its needs.
Rural Development Department is the nodal department, with Urban Development for urban women.
conditions: One woman per family resident in Bihar.
Apply with Aadhaar, income details and bank account; later assistance depends on review of the business started with the first grant.
items.onlyText: Only for women of Bihar (one woman per family)
apply: Apply online or through the block/JEEViKA office (Rural Development Department, Bihar)

items.name: Bihar Startup Policy 2022 (seed fund)
items.summary: Interest-free seed loan of ₹10 lakh for 10 years for recognised Bihar startups, plus ₹3 lakh accelerator support
details: Seed fund of ₹10 lakh as an interest-free loan for 10 years.
₹3 lakh extra for product development and training when the startup joins an accelerator programme.
Success fee of 2% of angel funds raised, and access to a matching loan through a state trust fund under the Industries Department.
items.extraFor: Women founders get 5% more (seed fund ₹10.5 lakh); SC/ST founders get 15% more (seed fund ₹11.5 lakh).
conditions: Startup registered in Bihar and recognised by the Bihar Startup cell.
Apply on the Startup Bihar portal; proposals are screened by an evaluation committee.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised under the Bihar Startup Policy

items.name: Bihar Agri Investment Promotion Policy (BAIPP) – capital subsidy for agro-processing
items.summary: 15% capital subsidy (25% for FPCs) on projects of ₹25 lakh to ₹5 crore; +5% SC/ST/EBC, +2% women
details: Credit-linked capital subsidy on eligible project cost for new units and for expansion that raises capacity by at least 25%.
Eligible sectors: makhana, honey, fruits and vegetables, maize, seeds, medicinal and aromatic plants, and tea.
Can be combined with the state industrial policy, but the same type of incentive cannot be claimed twice.
items.extraFor: SC, ST and EBC investors get 5% extra; women, acid-attack survivors, war widows, persons with disabilities and transgender investors get 2% extra
conditions: Sector: food/agro processing in the listed crops (NIC 10)
Bank or financial institution term loan of at least 20% of project cost is mandatory
Apply online to Bihar Horticulture Development Society (Agriculture Department)

items.name: Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy (Textile and Leather) 2022 – capital and interest support
items.summary: 15% capital subsidy on plant and machinery (up to ₹10 crore) plus 100% SGST refund for 5 years and interest subvention
details: Capital subsidy of 15% of plant and machinery cost, paid in five equal instalments, capped at ₹10 crore.
100% reimbursement of SGST deposited for 5 years.
Interest subvention under BIIPP 2016: 12% for micro and small units (10% for others) or actual rate, for up to 5 years.
100% stamp duty, registration and land-conversion fee exemption; patent support 50% up to ₹10 lakh; export freight 30% up to ₹10 lakh a year.
items.extraFor: SC/ST, women and differently abled entrepreneurs get a 5% higher incentive cap
conditions: Sector: weaving, knitting, apparel, hosiery, footwear and leather goods; spinning, processing, technical textiles and leather processing (NIC 13, 14, 15)
New units, or expansion/modernisation raising capacity by at least 25%
Policy runs five years from its June 2022 notification; apply for Stage I and financial clearance on the Bihar Single Window portal

items.name: Bihar Textile and Leather Policy 2022 – employment and power subsidy
items.summary: 300% of ESI/EPF paid for 5 years (₹3,000 to ₹5,000 per worker a month) and ₹2 per unit power subsidy
details: Employment subsidy for 5 years with monthly caps of ₹3,000 (semi-skilled), ₹4,000 (skilled) and ₹5,000 (highly skilled) per employee.
Power tariff subsidy of ₹2 per unit for 5 years, capped yearly at ₹2.5 lakh (micro), ₹12 lakh (small) and ₹35 lakh (medium).
Skill development subsidy of up to ₹20,000 per employee trained.
conditions: Only Category A units: weaving, knitting, apparel, garments, hosiery, footwear and leather garments (NIC 13, 14, 15)
At least 100 direct employees, 75% of them Bihar domicile
Apply on the Bihar Single Window portal

items.extraFor: Women pay 4% instead of 5%.
items.onlyText: Only for members of notified minority communities in Bihar
items.name: Mukhyamantri Alpsankhyak Rozgar Rin Yojana (Bihar State Minorities Financial Corporation)
items.summary: Self-employment loans up to ₹5 lakh at 5% simple interest (4% for women), repayable over 5 years
details: Repayment in 20 quarterly instalments after a 3-month moratorium; 0.5% interest rebate for full on-time repayment.
Applications are being taken for 2026-27.
conditions: Bihar resident from a notified minority community, aged 18 to 50, family income under ₹3 lakh a year.
Apply online on the Bihar minority welfare loan portal.

items.name: Bihar Purchase Preference Policy 2024
items.summary: Bihar MSEs and startups get up to 15% purchase-preference margin, free tender papers and EMD exemption in state tenders
details: Approved by the Bihar Cabinet on 6 Aug 2024; Urban Development Department told urban local bodies to apply it with immediate effect (Jul 2026).
Purchase preference margin of up to 15% for eligible Bihar enterprises in goods and services tenders.
Free tender documents, exemption from bid security (EMD), and up to 50% relaxation in turnover, age and experience criteria for specified categories.
Startups may get orders through nomination or limited tender in specified cases.
conditions: Enterprise registered in Bihar with an office there, operating in Bihar for at least one year and filing GST returns for at least one year.
For goods, the manufacturing unit must be in Bihar.

items.name: Powerloom electricity subsidy (Bihar Handloom and Sericulture Directorate)
items.summary: Subsidised electricity tariff for powerloom weavers, paid by the state directly to the power company
details: Rs 7.95 crore allocated in 2024-25; about 29,000 powerlooms in the state, 23,007 UID-registered.
Weavers are billed at the reduced rate; exact current rate per unit not confirmed.
conditions: Powerloom weaver using electricity for cloth production in Bihar; UID registration of the loom helps access benefits.
Contact the Directorate of Handloom and Sericulture or the district Udyog office.
items.onlyText: Only for powerloom weavers
apply: Bihar Directorate of Handloom and Sericulture

items.name: Working capital assistance for handloom weavers (Bihar)
items.summary: Working capital paid by DBT to handloom weavers for yarn and production (about Rs 15,000 per weaver in 2024-25)
details: Rs 4.25 crore given to 2,833 weavers in 2024-25.
Handloom Haat suppliers also get 25% of cloth value as sales support.
conditions: Handloom weavers in Bihar, including Pati-loom Kambal weavers.
Apply through the Directorate of Handloom and Sericulture / district Udyog office.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom weavers
apply: Bihar Directorate of Handloom and Sericulture

items.name: Bihar Khadi charkha and loom subsidy (Bihar State Khadi and Village Industries Board)
items.summary: 90% subsidy on charkhas and looms for khadi institutions and weavers; charkha loan of Rs 40,000 at 4% interest
details: Announced in September 2025 to help small khadi producers and weavers.
conditions: Khadi institutions and khadi weavers/spinners in Bihar.
Apply through the Bihar State Khadi and Village Industries Board (kvibbihar.com).
items.onlyText: Only for khadi institutions, spinners and weavers
apply: Bihar State Khadi and Village Industries Board

items.name: Bihar Tourism Policy 2023 (amended 2025): capital subsidy, SGST and employment incentives for hotels
items.summary: 25% capital subsidy for hotels (Rs 5 crore minimum for 2-star in smaller towns), SGST reimbursement for 7 years, EPF/ESIC support
details: 2025 amendment: 2-star hotels in sub-divisional towns and blocks qualify from Rs 5 crore investment; 3-star in district HQs from Rs 7.5 crore; 4-star in Patna, Gaya and Bodhgaya from Rs 10 crore (25% capital subsidy).
Units can choose capital subsidy or interest subvention under the policy guidelines.
SGST reimbursement period raised from 5 to 7 years.
Hotels hiring local people get 100% of employer EPF and ESIC contribution or Rs 3,000 per employee per month, whichever is lower; Rs 1,500 per month for hiring a disabled person from Bihar.
items.extraFor: Extra 5% capital subsidy at select locations
conditions: Policy in force for 5 years from G.O. No. 2825 dated 27 Dec 2023
Apply on the Bihar Tourism portal

items.name: Mukhyamantri Homestay Protsahan Yojana 2026 (Bihar)
items.summary: Rs 2.5 lakh per room for up to 4 rooms (max Rs 10 lakh), plus up to Rs 1 lakh extra for women, SHGs and young owners
details: Capital subsidy of Rs 2.5 lakh per room or actual approved cost, whichever is lower, for up to 4 rooms (homestay can register up to 8 rooms).
Covers new homestays, existing homestays and converted homes. Paid 50% after start of operations, 25% after one year and 25% after two years.
Runs FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
items.extraFor: Extra Rs 25,000 per room (max Rs 1 lakh) for women-run homestays, registered SHGs and owners aged 18 to 25
conditions: Bihar permanent resident who owns the property (or holds a 10-year registered lease)
Homestay within 5 km of one of 34 notified tourist destinations
Must run the homestay for at least 5 years
Apply online on the Bihar Tourism homestay portal; Rs 2,000 application fee

items.name: Bihar IT Policy 2024: capital subsidy, rent, power and EPF support for IT/ITeS/ESDM units
items.summary: 30% capital subsidy (up to Rs 30 crore) or 10% interest subvention for 5 years, plus 50% lease rent for 5 years
details: Capital subsidy of 30% of fixed capital investment up to Rs 30 crore, or instead 10% interest subvention for 5 years.
50% of lease rent for 5 years for units in leased offices; 25% of power bill for 5 years.
100% reimbursement of employer EPF and ESI contribution, up to Rs 5,000 per employee per month, for 5 years.
items.extraFor: Extra 5% for SC/ST/BC/EBC, women, Divyangjan, war widows, acid attack survivors and third-gender entrepreneurs; extra 10% outside Patna and Danapur
conditions: For IT, ITeS and ESDM units set up in Bihar
Apply to the Department of Information Technology, Bihar

states.statusText: Chandigarh has no UT fiscal incentive policy. Work on a new industrial policy began in Jul 2026.

portal.label: Chandigarh Administration, Department of Industries

states.notes: The 2015 policy offers facilitation only: a single window, time-bound clearances and self-certification.

items.name: Chandigarh Start-up Policy 2025
items.summary: Seed grant up to Rs 7 lakh and growth grant up to Rs 12 lakh (Rs 2 lakh extra for women-led), plus rent, patent and certification reimbursement
details: Idea grants of Rs 2 lakh (top 20) or Rs 1 lakh (next 50) with a year of incubation.
Seed/MVP grant up to Rs 7 lakh and early-growth grant up to Rs 12 lakh, 20 startups each per year; Rs 2 lakh extra for women- or transgender-led startups.
Rent Rs 5,000 a month for 12 months; 80% of IT/quality certification (up to Rs 1 lakh) and patent fees (up to Rs 10,000); event and accelerator support.
items.extraFor: Rs 2 lakh extra on seed and growth grants for women-led or transgender-led startups
conditions: DPIIT-recognised private limited company, partnership or LLP registered in Chandigarh (or GST-registered there).
Policy notified 29 Apr 2025 for 5 years; operational guidelines notified 1 Jan 2026.
Apply through a recognised incubator on the Start-In Chandigarh portal.
items.onlyText: Only for DPIIT-recognised startups registered in Chandigarh

states.statusText: In force (amended in 2025 and Jan 2026). Incentive applications must go through the One Click single window.

portal.label: One Click Single Window

states.zones: Rates depend on the development block: Group 1 (10 developed blocks), Group 2 (61) or Group 3 (75 least developed, highest rates).
states.notes: New units must start production between 1 Nov 2024 and 31 Mar 2030; expansion, diversification and modernisation get the same package. Services qualify only if listed, and trading is not covered. The policy uses plant-and-machinery size limits of ₹1/10/50 crore.

items.name: Fixed Capital Investment (FCI) subsidy
items.summary: FCI subsidy 30/35/40% in Groups 1/2/3; thrust-sector and service MSMEs get 35/40/45%.
details: Caps (₹ lakh) Groups 1/2/3 - general: micro 30/35/40, small 250/350/450, medium 400/450/500; thrust and services: micro 35/40/45, small 350/450/550, medium 700/750/800. FCI covers land development, building, plant & machinery, power and water supply. Alternative to Net SGST reimbursement.
items.extraFor: Women, ex-servicemen, retired Agniveers, Naxal-affected, divyang (also NRIs, exporters): subsidy and cap raised by 10% of the general amount. SC/ST: separate Chapter D-1 package, rates unconfirmed
conditions: Choose either FCI subsidy or Net SGST reimbursement
Udyam Aakanksha before production; production certificate after
Services only if in the eligible service list
Thrust status needs sector minimum investment

items.name: Interest subsidy on term loan
items.summary: Interest subsidy 40/45/50% for 5/6/7 years (general); 45/50/55% for 6/7/8 years (thrust, services).
details: Annual caps (₹ lakh) Groups 1/2/3 - general: micro 15/20/25, small 25/30/35, medium 35/40/45; thrust and services: micro 20/25/30, small 30/35/40, medium 40/45/50.
items.extraFor: Special categories (see FCI subsidy): +10% of subsidy and cap
conditions: Term loan from bank/financial institution

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement (alternative to FCI subsidy)
items.summary: Net SGST reimbursed for 5/7/9 years up to 75% of FCI (general MSMEs).
details: General MSME: Groups 1/2/3 - 5/7/9 years, ceiling 75% of FCI. Thrust: 6/8/10 years, ceiling 100% of FCI. Services: 10 years, ceiling 150% of FCI (not group-wise). Enterprise must choose either Net SGST or FCI subsidy.
items.extraFor: Special categories: +10% of amount and one extra year
conditions: Mutually exclusive with FCI subsidy

items.name: Electricity duty exemption
items.summary: 100% electricity duty exemption for 5/7/9 years by block group (thrust, services 6/8/10).
details: From commencement of commercial production; new MSMEs only. General: 5/7/9 years (Groups 1/2/3); thrust: 6/8/10 years; services: up to 6/8/10 years.
items.extraFor: Special categories: one extra year
conditions: New enterprise only

items.name: Stamp duty exemption
items.summary: 100% stamp duty exemption on land/shed/building purchase or lease deeds and loan documents.
details: Deeds for purchase/lease of land, shed or buildings (excluding mining leases) and loan/advance deeds executed within 3 years of loan sanction; same in all block groups.

items.name: Margin money subsidy and SC/ST land-premium waiver
items.summary: 25% margin money subsidy, up to ₹100 lakh, for special-category micro and small entrepreneurs.
details: On capital investment up to ₹10 crore for new micro/small units of SC/ST, women, ex-servicemen, retired Agniveer, Naxal-affected, third-gender and divyang entrepreneurs. SC/ST also get 100% land-premium exemption in DI/CSIDC industrial areas with lease rent ₹1 per acre per year.
items.extraFor: SC/ST, women, ex-servicemen, retired Agniveers, Naxal-affected, third gender, divyang
conditions: New micro or small unit
items.onlyText: Only for SC/ST, women, ex-servicemen, retired Agniveer, Naxal-affected, third-gender or divyang entrepreneurs

items.name: Land diversion fee exemption
items.summary: 50% exemption on industrial land diversion fee for micro and small units, up to 15 acres.
details: 50% of land diversion fee for industrial purpose, maximum 15 acres.

items.name: Project report, quality, patent, technology and listing support
items.summary: Quality certification 50% up to ₹10 lakh; patent 50% up to ₹20 lakh; technology purchase 50% up to ₹10 lakh.
details: Project report: 1% of FCI, max ₹10 lakh. Water/energy audit: 50%, max ₹5 lakh. SME-exchange listing: 50%, max ₹10 lakh.

items.name: Employment and training subsidy
items.summary: 40% of net salary for five years (max ₹5 lakh/year) for hiring divyang, retired Agniveers, surrendered Naxalites.
details: Also training reimbursement of one month's wage or ₹15,000 per person, whichever is less, for five years. The 75% EPF reimbursement is for large units only, not MSMEs.
conditions: Salary subsidy only for the listed employee groups

items.name: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swarozgar Yojana (MYSY)
items.summary: Margin money grant 10–25% (max ₹1–1.5 lakh) plus 5–8% interest subsidy for 5 years on loans up to ₹25 lakh
details: Bank loan limits: manufacturing up to ₹25 lakh, services up to ₹10 lakh, trading up to ₹2 lakh.
Interest subsidy for 5 years: general 5% (caps ₹50,000/yr term loan, ₹25,000/yr working capital); special categories 8% (caps ₹75,000 and ₹40,000).
Credit guarantee fee and annual service fee support for 4 years.
Run by the Commerce & Industries Department through District Trade and Industry Centres (DTIC).
items.extraFor: Margin money 15% (max ₹1.5 lakh) for OBC, minority, women, disabled, ex-servicemen and Naxal-affected; 25% (max ₹1.5 lakh) for SC/ST; 8% interest subsidy for special categories; 5-year age relaxation
conditions: Native of Chhattisgarh, at least Class 8 pass, age 18 to 35, family income up to ₹3 lakh a year, one person per family
Not a loan defaulter and no earlier subsidy under PMRY/PMEGP or similar schemes
Submit form and project profile to the DTIC; task force interview, then bank sanction

states.notes: Units not yet producing can opt once for the 2022 scheme by 25 Mar 2027. A services MSME scheme is still awaited. State and central support together are capped at eligible fixed capital investment.

items.name: Capital subsidy (Component 1)
items.summary: 35% of eligible fixed capital investment in Category A talukas, 25% in Category B.
details: Micro: paid in year 1 (annual cap 37% A/27% B of EFCI, then 2% a year). Small/medium: paid over 5 years (annual cap 9% A/7% B). Thrust sectors (toys, sports goods, footwear, robots, drones): 35% A/30% B. Components 1-3 combined are capped at 45% A/35% B of EFCI (thrust sectors 50%/45%).
conditions: Manufacturing/job work only; services and trading excluded
Self-financed projects eligible; land, working capital and second-hand assets excluded
Assets bought from 2026-01-01; provisional certificate within 6 months of production, final within 6 months of completion; up to 2 years late with a pro-rata cut
Expansion needs +50% gross fixed capital investment (60% of it in plant and machinery) and +50% capacity; diversification needs +25% (micro/small) or +50% (medium)
85% Gujarat-domiciled workforce

items.name: Interest subsidy (Component 2)
items.summary: 7% interest subsidy on term loans for 5 years, up to 10% of EFCI (thrust sectors 20%).
details: Counts within the combined 45%/35% ceiling. The enterprise bears at least 2%; penal interest excluded. The GR scan is garbled at this number; 7% comes from ADAPT's reading of the GR and other summaries.
items.extraFor: +1% for women entrepreneurs, registered manufacturing startups and first-generation entrepreneurs
conditions: Disbursed term loans only

items.name: Power tariff support (Component 3)
items.summary: ₹2 per unit (Category A) or ₹1 per unit (Category B) for 5 years, up to 25% of EFCI.
details: Thrust sectors: same rates, capped at 20% of EFCI. Power from the DISCOM or open-access renewables only; captive generation excluded. Expansion units get it only on additional consumption. Counts within the combined ceiling.
conditions: Claims start after the provisional eligibility certificate

items.name: EPF reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of the employer's EPF contribution for new employees, for 5 years from production.
details: Cap per employee: 12% of basic+DA, or ₹1,800/month (men), ₹2,500 (women), ₹3,000 (specially-abled), whichever is lower. A new employee is one with no UAN before joining.
items.extraFor: Higher caps for women (₹2,500) and specially-abled (₹3,000) employees
conditions: New employees only

items.name: Electricity duty exemption
items.summary: Electricity duty exemption as applicable under the Gujarat Electricity Duty Act, 1958.
details: Secondary summaries call it 100%; the duration is not stated in the GR text read.

items.name: Quality, technology and IP support
items.summary: Quality certification 50% up to ₹10 lakh; patents 75% up to ₹25 lakh; technology acquisition 65% up to ₹50 lakh.
details: ERP 65% ≤₹1L; ICT/Industry 4.0 65% ≤₹5L; ZED 50% (after GoI aid) ≤₹50,000; energy/water audit 75% ≤₹50,000 each; recommended equipment 25% ≤₹20L (needs ≥10% savings).
conditions: Apply within 6 months of installation or certificate

items.name: Rent assistance
items.summary: 65% of rent for a rented or leased shed, up to ₹3 lakh a year for 5 years.
details: 75% if 100% women-owned, same ₹3 lakh/year cap. Runs 5 years from commercial production.
items.extraFor: 75% for 100% women-owned units
conditions: Apply within 6 months of the rent agreement
Coverage of medium units unconfirmed

items.name: CGTMSE fee, SME listing and power connection support
items.summary: CGTMSE fee 100% for 5 years; SME listing 25% up to ₹5 lakh; power connection 35% up to ₹5 lakh.
details: CGTMSE annual fee reimbursed on collateral-free loans (micro/small). Power connection charges covered for new or additional load outside GIDC estates.

items.name: Stamp duty reimbursement and extras (thrust sectors only)
items.summary: Thrust-sector MSMEs: 100% reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges on project land.
details: Only toys, sports goods, footwear, robots and drones. Other thrust-sector extras: IPR 75% ≤₹1 Cr; international certification 100% ≤₹5 Cr; training ₹8,000/employee/month for 12 months; design studio 50% ≤₹5 Cr.
conditions: Apply within 6 months of production

items.name: SC/ST additional support (separate schemes)
items.summary: SC/ST extras are in separate Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar (SC) and Bhagwan Birsa Munda (ST) schemes, not this GR.
details: One secondary source cites an extra 5% ceiling for SC/ST entrepreneurs. The 2026 versions of these schemes were not located.
items.extraFor: SC/ST
items.onlyText: Only for SC/ST entrepreneurs

items.name: Shri Vajpayee Bankable Yojana
items.summary: Bank loans up to ₹25 lakh with state subsidy up to ₹3.75 lakh for small industry, service and business units
details: Loan limit raised from ₹8 lakh to ₹25 lakh and subsidy cap from ₹1.25 lakh to ₹3.75 lakh under the Cottage and Rural Industries Policy (Nov 2024).
Run by the Commissionerate of Cottage and Rural Industries through District Industries Centres; banks sanction the loans.
items.extraFor: Higher subsidy rates for women, SC/ST, differently abled and other special categories (rates not confirmed)
conditions: Gujarat resident aged 18 to 65; passed 4th standard or has relevant training/experience; no income limit.
Apply online on the e-Kutir portal; DIC forwards to bank.

items.name: Manav Kalyan Yojana (toolkit assistance)
items.summary: Free trade toolkits via e-voucher for small self-employment trades such as tailoring, repair, beauty parlour, papad making
details: Toolkits for listed trades (about 28), redeemed at approved dealers using e-vouchers; optional skill training.
Run by the Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries.
conditions: Gujarat resident aged 18 to 60; family income up to ₹6 lakh (no income limit for some SC/ST and nomadic groups).
Apply on the e-Kutir portal.
items.onlyText: Only for low-income individuals starting small trades

items.name: Gujarat Scheme for Assistance for Start-ups / Innovation (seed support and sustenance allowance)
items.summary: Seed grant up to ₹30 lakh (plus ₹10 lakh for high-impact) and allowance up to ₹20,000/month for a year (₹25,000 with a woman co-founder)
details: Support through state-recognised Nodal Institutes, including incubation and mentoring.
Extra 1% interest subsidy on eligible term loans and support for accelerator programmes.
items.extraFor: Sustenance allowance ₹25,000/month if a co-founder is a woman
conditions: Gujarat-based startup (LLP, partnership or private company) up to 10 years old, turnover up to ₹100 crore, recommended by a Nodal Institute.
Apply through a recognised Nodal Institute under the 2020 scheme guidelines.

items.name: Gujarat Textile Policy 2024 (capital, interest, payroll and power support)
items.summary: Capital subsidy 10-35% of eligible fixed capital, 5-7% interest subsidy for 5-8 years, ₹1/kWh power support for 5 years
details: Payroll assistance per worker per month (higher for women) and training assistance.
Support for quality certification, energy and water saving, and technology acquisition.
Covers garments, made-ups, technical textiles, weaving, knitting, processing, texturising, twisting, embroidery; cotton spinning excluded.
conditions: New or expanding textile units in Gujarat in eligible segments.
Apply to the Industries Commissionerate under the policy guidelines.

items.name: Gujarat IT/ITeS Policy 2022-27: CAPEX and OPEX support
items.summary: 25% CAPEX support (cap Rs 50 cr) and 15% yearly OPEX support (cap Rs 20 cr/yr for 5 years) for IT/ITeS units
details: CAPEX: up to 25% of eligible capital expenditure, cap Rs 50 crore (Category I, investment under Rs 250 crore), paid in 20 quarterly instalments.
OPEX: up to 15% of eligible annual operating expenses (lease rental, bandwidth, cloud rental, power tariff, patent costs) for 5 years, cap Rs 20 crore a year.
Interest assistance up to 7% (unit bears at least 2%), cap Rs 1 crore a year for 5 years; 100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years.
Policy dated 7 Feb 2022, valid to 31 Mar 2027.
conditions: New or expanding IT/ITeS units in Gujarat; existing units had to register on the portal to claim expansion incentives.
Apply on the DST Gujarat policy portal.

items.name: Gujarat IT/ITeS Policy 2022-27: Employment Generation Incentive
items.summary: One month's CTC (50%) per new local hire: up to Rs 50,000 per male and Rs 60,000 per female employee
details: One-time 50% of one month's cost-to-company per new local employee retained for at least a year; caps Rs 50,000 (male) and Rs 60,000 (female).
Eligibility for new hires runs to 31 Mar 2027.
Upskilling support for employees: up to Rs 50,000 or 50% of course fee by DBT.
conditions: IT/ITeS unit registered under the policy; claim once per employee.
Apply on the DST Gujarat policy portal.

items.name: Gujarat Electronics Policy 2022-28 (ESDM units)
items.summary: 20% capital assistance, 7% interest aid for 5 years, Re 1/unit power subsidy, 100% stamp duty and EPF support for electronics units
details: Capital assistance: 20% of eligible capital expenditure, overall cap Rs 200 crore (lower rate for larger investments).
Interest assistance up to 7% (unit bears at least 2%) for 5 years, cap Rs 10 crore a year.
100% reimbursement of stamp duty and registration fees on land; Re 1 per unit power subsidy for 5 years plus electricity duty exemption.
EPF reimbursement for 5 years: 100% for women employees, 75% for men.
Apply by 31 Mar 2028; operations must start by 31 Mar 2031.
conditions: Electronics system design and manufacturing units in Gujarat with Udyam registration or IEM.
Apply on the DST Gujarat policy portal.

items.extraFor: Women in the higher income band pay 6% instead of 8%.
items.onlyText: Only for religious and linguistic minority applicants in Gujarat
items.name: Term Loan Scheme (Gujarat Minorities Finance and Development Corporation, GMFDC)
items.summary: Self-employment term loans of ₹1 lakh to ₹20 lakh at 6% to 8% for minority entrepreneurs
details: 6% for family income up to ₹1.2 lakh; above that and up to ₹8 lakh, 8% for men and 6% for women.
Repayment in 60 monthly instalments; covers services, skilled self-employment, handicrafts, transport and allied activities.
conditions: Gujarat resident from a religious minority (or Sindhi, Marathi, Urdu linguistic minority), aged 21 to 45, family income up to ₹8 lakh.
No existing loan from GMFDC or another government lender; experience or technical training in the trade.
Apply online on the GMFDC portal or at the district social welfare office.

items.onlyText: Only for Thakor and Koli community members in Gujarat
items.name: Term Loan Scheme (Gujarat Thakor and Koli Vikas Nigam, GTKVN)
items.summary: Self-employment loans up to ₹10 lakh (6% up to ₹5 lakh) for Thakor and Koli community members
details: Nigam funds 95% of project cost; the borrower brings 5% margin money. Repayment in 60 monthly instalments.
At least half of the loan budget is reserved for families earning up to ₹1.5 lakh.
conditions: Gujarat resident of the Thakor or Koli community, aged 21 to 50, family income up to ₹3 lakh, with skill or experience in the trade.
One guarantor and suitable collateral required; apply online on the GTKVN portal.

items.name: Gujarat Procurement Policy 2024 (MSME and women-enterprise preferences)
items.summary: State purchase policy from 1 Apr 2024 with special incentives for MSMEs, women-run units, startups and SC/ST firms
details: Announced 16 Mar 2024; applies from 1 Apr 2024 to purchases of goods and services by state departments, boards, corporations, societies and grant-in-aid bodies.
Gives special incentives to MSMEs and women entrepreneurs; startups are exempted from some qualifying criteria; SC/ST-run enterprises are also supported.
Replaces Purchase Policy 2016, which gave registered micro, small and cottage units EMD and tender-fee exemption and a 10% price preference; current figures not confirmed.
items.extraFor: Separate incentives for women-run and SC/ST enterprises (amounts not confirmed).
conditions: Unit registered in Gujarat with Udyam registration; products to meet BIS specifications.
Purchases are encouraged through GeM; check tender terms for the MSME and women-enterprise relaxations.

items.name: Mahila Swavlamban Yojana (Gujarat Women Economic Development Corporation)
items.summary: Loan up to Rs 2 lakh for BPL women to start or expand a business, with 15% subsidy up to Rs 30,000
details: Women and Child Development Department scheme run through the Gujarat Women Economic Development Corporation.
Loan up to Rs 2 lakh to start or expand an economic activity.
Subsidy of 15% of project cost, capped at Rs 30,000.
conditions: Woman resident of Gujarat from a BPL family, within the scheme income limit.
Apply offline to the Women Economic Development Corporation with age proof, Aadhaar, quotation, experience certificate, income proof and ration card.
items.onlyText: Only for women from BPL families
apply: Women and Child Development Department, Gujarat

items.name: Dattopant Thengadi Artisan Interest Subsidy Scheme (Gujarat Cottage Policy 2024)
items.summary: Interest subsidy on bank loans to handloom and handicraft artisans; loan cap raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 3 lakh
details: Cap raised under the Gujarat Cottage Policy announced in November 2024 (valid five years).
Interest subsidy rate not confirmed from official text.
conditions: Registered handloom or handicraft artisan in Gujarat (artisan card from the Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries).
Apply online on the e-Kutir portal; loan through a bank.
items.onlyText: Only for registered handloom and handicraft artisans
apply: e-Kutir portal, Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries

items.name: Craft Business Development Scheme (Gujarat cottage industries)
items.summary: 70% state assistance on craft-cluster projects up to Rs 7 crore over 10 years (tools, design, raw material bank, marketing, exports)
details: Components: diagnostic study and DPR, tools and equipment, design and product diversification, raw material bank, marketing, publicity and export help.
G.R. dated 26 December 2016, amended 26 November 2020.
conditions: Clusters or centres of 100 to 300 artisans, run in a public-private model.
Apply to the Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries.
items.onlyText: Only for artisan clusters of 100 to 300 artisans
apply: Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries

items.name: Scheme for Granting Assistance to Processing Units in APMC (General Area)
items.summary: One-time capital subsidy of 25% (A/B class APMC areas) or 50% (C/D class) of fixed capital, up to ₹1.5 crore
details: Supports grading, sorting, cleaning, packaging and value-addition units for agricultural produce set up in the general (non-tribal) area of an APMC.
Assistance is 25% of fixed capital investment in 'A' and 'B' class market committee areas and 50% in 'C' and 'D' class areas, up to ₹1.5 crore.
conditions: Run by the Gujarat Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation Department; aimed mainly at co-operative societies, check whether private units qualify.
Apply offline to the District Registrar (co-operative societies) office.
items.onlyText: Mainly for co-operative societies in Gujarat

states.short: Haryana Progressive MSME and Export Promotion Policy 2026
states.statusText: Notified 29 Jul 2026; operational guidelines are awaited. Rates below come from a consultant's summary of the gazette.

portal.label: Invest Haryana (MSME Directorate: msme.haryana.gov.in)

states.zones: Rates depend on the site: Core (inside municipal limits), Intermediate, Sub-Prime, or Prime/Focus (notified promotion zones).
states.notes: Replaces the MSME Policy 2019 and HEEP-2020. Extra support for women, SC, PwD, ex-servicemen, Agniveers and first-generation entrepreneurs was announced; amounts are unconfirmed.

items.name: Capital investment subsidy (thrust sectors)
items.summary: Thrust-sector manufacturing: capital subsidy of 15–30% by area category, max ₹2–4 crore.
details: Core 15% (max ₹2 crore); Intermediate 20% (₹2.5 crore); Sub-Prime 25% (₹3.5 crore); Prime/Focus 30% (₹4 crore).
Thrust sectors: auto, aerospace & defence, general engineering, electrical/electronics, pharma, rubber & plastic, footwear & leather, renewable energy, textile & apparel.
conditions: Manufacturing projects in the 9 thrust sectors only
New, expansion and diversification projects qualify
All state incentives for a project capped at 100% of FCI
Operational guidelines reported pending at launch

items.name: Interest subsidy for micro and small units
items.summary: Micro and small units: 5–7% interest subsidy by area, max ₹20–25 lakh a year.
details: Core 5% (max ₹20 lakh a year); Intermediate 6% (₹20 lakh a year); Sub-Prime and Prime/Focus 7% (₹25 lakh a year). Duration unconfirmed.
conditions: Services eligibility and expansion eligibility unconfirmed

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement
items.summary: Net SGST reimbursement of 20–70% for 7 years, depending on area and share of in-state B2C sales.
details: If ≥50% of sales are B2C within Haryana: Core 30%, Intermediate 50%, Sub-Prime 60%, Prime/Focus 70%. Otherwise: 20%, 40%, 50%, 60%.
conditions: Sector limits and expansion eligibility unconfirmed

items.name: Stamp duty refund
items.summary: Stamp duty refund of 30–100% by area category.
details: Core 30%; Intermediate 60%; Sub-Prime 75%; Prime/Focus 100%.
conditions: Expansion eligibility unconfirmed

items.name: Employment generation assistance
items.summary: ₹1–1.2 lakh per employee per year for hiring Haryana youth (reported).
details: From launch coverage; eligibility, duration and caps unconfirmed.
conditions: Terms unconfirmed

items.name: Certification, testing and automation support
items.summary: Certifications 50% (max ₹10 lakh a year); international 60% (₹20 lakh); testing equipment 50% (₹25 lakh); automation 25%.
details: Standard certifications: 50% up to ₹10 lakh a year for 3 years. International certifications: 60% up to ₹20 lakh (2 years). Testing equipment: 50% up to ₹25 lakh, twice per policy. Automation/robotics: 25% (₹50 lakh–₹1 crore).

items.name: Market development, e-commerce and export support
items.summary: Trade fairs 25% (₹3–5 lakh); e-commerce fees 75% (₹1–2 lakh a year, 5 years); export incentives.
details: Export credit: 3% subvention up to ₹10 lakh a year for 3 years. New ZED-certified MSE exporters: freight aid of 1% of FOB (₹10/15/30 lakh a year by area). First-time exporters: 33% up to ₹20 lakh a year for 3 years.
conditions: Fairs up to 3 times a year

items.name: MSE insurance scheme
items.summary: Micro and small units: 33% of insurance premium reimbursed, up to ₹5 lakh a year for 3 years.
details: New MSE insurance scheme under the 2026 policy.

items.name: PADMA Designing, Branding, Marketing and Exports Promotion Scheme
items.summary: 50% reimbursement of branding, digital marketing, e-commerce and export promotion costs, up to ₹10 lakh a year
details: Covers logo and packaging design, sustainable packaging, digital marketing, e-commerce listing, market intelligence and export promotion.
Part of the five-year PADMA programme (₹150 crore in the 2026-27 budget); announced Sep 2026.
conditions: Micro and small enterprises in identified PADMA products/clusters (one block, one product).
Cannot claim another state scheme for the same purpose.
apply: Department of Industries and Commerce, Haryana

items.name: Haryana Matrushakti Udyamita Yojana
items.summary: Collateral-free bank loans up to ₹5 lakh for women starting a business
details: Loans up to ₹5 lakh with a three-month moratorium, through the Haryana Women Development Corporation.
Interest subvention rate not confirmed.
conditions: Women aged 18 to 60 with family income below ₹5 lakh a year.
Apply at the Women Development Corporation district office with Aadhaar, Parivar Pehchan Patra, income certificate and business details.
items.onlyText: Only women aged 18 to 60 with family income below ₹5 lakh
apply: Haryana Women Development Corporation district office

items.name: Haryana State Startup Policy 2022 incentives
items.summary: Seed grant up to ₹10 lakh, 30% lease rental (45% for women-led, max ₹5 lakh) and patent cost reimbursement up to ₹25 lakh
details: Seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh per startup.
Lease rental reimbursement of 30% (45% for women-led startups), up to ₹5 lakh, for one year.
100% of patent costs: up to ₹3 lakh per national and ₹10 lakh per international patent, ₹25 lakh in all over 5 years.

50% net SGST reimbursement for 7 years (up to 100% of fixed capital investment), 75% of cloud storage costs at Haryana data centres (up to ₹2.5 lakh a year for 5 years), and up to ₹2.5 lakh a year for national acceleration programmes.
Electricity duty exemption for 7 to 12 years depending on block category.
items.extraFor: Women-led startups get 45% lease rental support instead of 30%
conditions: Startup registered and recognised on the Startup Haryana portal (Industries and Commerce Department).
Claim incentives online on the Startup Haryana portal.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised under the Haryana State Startup Policy

items.name: Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy 2022-25 – capital investment subsidy for textile units
