items.summary: 35% to 40% capital subsidy, up to ₹2.5 crore to ₹5 crore by block and segment
details: All textile units: 35% up to ₹2.5 crore (Block B), 40% up to ₹3.5 crore (Blocks C and D).
Technical textiles and backward integration: up to ₹3.5 crore (B) or ₹5 crore (C, D); open-end spinning 40% up to ₹4 crore; textile machinery 30% up to ₹2 crore.
Also net SGST-linked investment subsidy (25% for 8 years in Block B, 50% for 10 years in C and D) and stamp duty refund of 80% to 100%.
Policy extended to 18 Dec 2026 and the cap on number of cases was removed.
conditions: Sector: textiles and apparel, technical textiles, textile machinery (NIC 13, 14, 2826)
New units or expansion/diversification above 25% of existing fixed capital, finished within 18 months
Not available in Block A (most developed) areas
Apply on the Haryana MSME / HEPC portal before 18 Dec 2026

items.name: Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy 2022-25 – interest subsidy for textile MSMEs
items.summary: 6% to 7% interest subsidy on term loans for 7 years, up to ₹20 lakh to ₹50 lakh a year
details: 6% up to ₹20 lakh a year in Block B; 7% up to ₹30 lakh a year in Block C; 7% up to ₹50 lakh a year in Block D.
Textile machinery MSMEs: 6% up to ₹25 lakh a year (B, C) or ₹40 lakh a year (D), anywhere in the state.
Policy extended to 18 Dec 2026.
conditions: Textile MSMEs (NIC 13, 14) setting up, expanding or modernising
Term loan from a bank or financial institution
Apply on the Haryana MSME portal

items.name: Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy 2022-25 – green and sustainable production support
items.summary: Up to 75% of ETP/ZLD cost (ZLD up to ₹10 crore), solar rooftop 30% to 50% and 75% energy/water audit cost
details: ETP for textile MSMEs 75% up to ₹1 crore (Block D); ZLD 40% to 75% up to ₹10 crore.
Energy-saving equipment 20% to 50% up to ₹20 lakh; water-saving equipment 50% up to ₹20 lakh.
Energy audit 75% up to ₹2 lakh and water audit 75% up to ₹1 lakh, paid when recommendations are implemented.
Solar rooftop 30% up to ₹20 lakh (Blocks A, B), 50% up to ₹40 lakh (C) and ₹50 lakh (D).
conditions: Textile units in Haryana (NIC 13, 14)
Policy extended to 18 Dec 2026
Apply on the Haryana MSME portal

items.onlyText: Only for Scheduled Caste applicants (NSKFDC loans only for sanitation workers and dependents)
items.name: HSFDC bank-linked self-employment schemes (Haryana SC Finance and Development Corporation)
items.summary: Bank loans for SC units up to ₹1.5 lakh project cost with 50% subsidy (max ₹50,000) and 10% margin money at 4%
details: Covers industrial units (carpentry, leather, handloom, flour mill, welding), trade and business (shops, tea stalls, auto repair, beauty parlour, tent house) and professional or self-employment ventures.
Corporation margin money carries 4% a year; the bank finances the balance at its own rate.
Separate NSKFDC-funded loans up to ₹2 lakh at 6% to 8% with subsidy up to ₹50,000 for sanitation workers and their dependents (e-rickshaw/CNG auto Green Business, women's schemes).
conditions: Permanent Haryana resident, Scheduled Caste, aged 18 to 55, family income up to ₹3 lakh (family ID); no dues to the corporation or a bank.
Register and apply online on the HSFDC portal, or at credit camps run by the Deputy Commissioner's office.

items.name: Haryana State Public Procurement Policy for MSEs
items.summary: Haryana MSEs get purchase preference up to 50% of tendered quantity, no EMD and no tender fee
details: Announced Oct 2016 by the Haryana Finance Department.
Purchase preference for up to 50% of the total tendered quantity to Haryana MSEs.
EMD (earlier 2% of tender value) removed; tender fee nil for eligible MSEs; 90% concession in performance security.
Turnover criteria relaxed by 80% for micro and 70% for small units.
conditions: Manufacturing MSE (including khadi and village units) registered in Haryana.
Quality certification (ISI, ISO, Agmark) or registration with NSIC or a government buyer may be required.

items.name: Haryana Logistics, Warehousing and Retail Policy 2019 (extended): incentives for warehouses and logistics units
items.summary: Capital subsidy, interest subsidy, stamp duty reimbursement and electricity duty exemption for logistics and warehousing units
details: Offers capital subsidy, interest subsidy, stamp duty reimbursement, electricity duty exemption and capacity-building support for logistics, warehousing and retail units.
The 2019 policy expired on 8 March 2024; the Cabinet extended it and its schemes until the new Logistics, Warehousing and Retail Policy 2024 is notified.
Exact rates and caps not confirmed. The 2023 draft of the new policy proposed 25% capital subsidy up to Rs 5 crore in C and D category blocks.
conditions: Warehousing units can also take MSME policy incentives, but not net SGST refund (as per draft)
Apply on the HEPC / Invest Haryana single-window portal

items.name: Haryana Agri-Business and Food Processing Policy 2026: capital investment subsidy for food processing units
items.summary: 25% capital investment subsidy for new or expanding agro and food processing units, capped at ₹2 to 4 crore by zone
details: Notified 29 May 2026 (No. 02/02/2026-1IB-II) for five years, replacing the 2018 policy.
New and expanding agro and food processing units get 25% capital investment subsidy, with the cap (₹2 crore to ₹4 crore) depending on the location zone.
items.extraFor: Extra 5% for units led by women, SC, Divyang, transgender persons or ex-servicemen
conditions: Administered by the Industries and Commerce Department, Haryana; zone-wise caps and eligibility are in the notification.
Apply online on the Haryana industries portal.

items.name: Haryana Agri-Business and Food Processing Policy 2026: cold chain, linkage, testing lab and food waste grants
items.summary: 35-45% grants: cold chain up to ₹6 crore, farm-to-market linkages up to ₹5 crore, food testing labs up to ₹2.5 crore
details: Integrated cold chain (for example IQF lines, blast freezers): 35% to 45% subsidy, up to ₹6 crore.
Backward and forward linkages (aggregation, pack houses, retail distribution): up to 35%, capped at ₹5 crore.
Food testing labs: 45% grant up to ₹2.5 crore; R&D or incubation centres: 45% up to ₹5 crore; food waste processing: 45% up to ₹2 crore.
items.extraFor: Extra 5% for units led by women, SC, Divyang, transgender persons or ex-servicemen
conditions: Policy valid five years from 29 May 2026.
Projects already funded by central grants for the same items are usually excluded; check the notification.
Apply online on the Haryana industries portal.

states.statusText: The extension to 12 Oct 2026 has ended. No further extension or new Industrial Policy 2026 had been announced by 24 Oct 2026; check with the Department of Industries before relying on these incentives.

portal.label: HP Single Window (Emerging Himachal)

states.zones: Category A (developed), B (developing) or C (tribal areas and backward blocks and panchayats); benefits rise from A to C.
states.notes: Every incentive needs at least 80% Himachali employees. Trading is not covered; services qualify only if listed in Annexure II.

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement
items.summary: Net SGST reimbursed 60% (Cat A) or 90% (Cat B/C) for 7 years, capped at 100% of FCI.
details: MSMEs other than steel: 60% in A, 90% in B and C, for 7 years, capped at 100% of fixed capital investment. Steel manufacturers: 50% A, 80% B, 90% C.
conditions: New enterprise, or substantial expansion (plant and machinery value up at least 25%)
At least 80% bonafide Himachali employees
Commercial production by the extended deadline of 12 Oct 2026 (no later extension announced yet)
Negative list (Annexure-III) excluded; services only if on the Annexure-II list

items.name: Interest subvention on term loans
items.summary: 3% interest subvention on term loans for 3 years; max ₹2L, ₹4L or ₹6L per year (A/B/C).
details: 3% interest subvention on term loans for 3 years, capped at ₹2 lakh (A), ₹4 lakh (B) or ₹6 lakh (C) per year.
items.extraFor: Special-category owners (SC, ST, BPL, women, ex-servicemen, persons with disabilities, people affected by HIV/AIDS): 5% for 5 years, capped at ₹3L, ₹5L or ₹7L per year (A/B/C).
conditions: Same eligibility conditions as the SGST reimbursement

items.name: Stamp duty and registration fee concession
items.summary: Stamp duty and registration fee charged at 50% (A), 30% (B) or 10% (C) of normal rates.
details: Stamp duty and registration fee are charged at 50% (A), 30% (B) and 10% (C) of normal rates, meaning a 50%, 70% or 90% concession.
conditions: Same eligibility conditions as the SGST reimbursement

items.name: Concession on industrial land and sheds
items.summary: 50%, 60% or 70% concession (A/B/C) on the premium for government industrial land or sheds.
details: 50% (A), 60% (B) or 70% (C) off the fixed rate or premium for land or industrial sheds. MSME plots are paid 12% upfront plus 8 annual interest-free instalments. Production must start within 2 years of possession (1 year for sheds).
items.extraFor: Persons with disabilities get out-of-turn plot allotment.
conditions: Plots and sheds in Department of Industries industrial areas

items.name: Concessional electricity duty
items.summary: Electricity duty for 5 years of 1% (up to 50 kVA) or 3% (51–100 kVA).
details: Electricity duty for 5 years: 1% for small industrial consumers (up to 50 kVA), 3% for medium (51–100 kVA), 5% for large supply. Normal rates apply afterwards.
conditions: Same eligibility conditions as the SGST reimbursement

items.name: Concessional energy charges
items.summary: New enterprises pay energy charges 15% below the approved tariff for 3 years.
details: New enterprises: energy charges 15% below the approved tariff for 3 years. Substantial expansion: 15% rebate on the added consumption for 3 years. Given through the yearly tariff schedule and stated as not binding on the State.
conditions: Subject to the annual electricity tariff order

items.name: Transport subsidy (Category B and C areas)
items.summary: Transport costs reimbursed up to 3% (B) or 5% (C) of turnover, max ₹10 lakh a year.
details: Pays actual transport cost of raw material and finished goods within HP, or 3% of turnover (Cat B, 3 years) or 5% (Cat C, 5 years), whichever is lower. Max ₹10 lakh a year. Not available in Cat A.
conditions: Category B or C location only

items.name: Quality certification and patent support
items.summary: 50% of in-house testing setup cost for certification (max ₹5 lakh); patents: 75%, max ₹10 lakh.
details: 50% of the cost of in-house testing facilities for BIS, WHO-GMP, ISO or organic certification, max ₹5 lakh per enterprise. Patents: 75% of attorney and filing charges or ₹10 lakh, whichever is lower.
conditions: Same eligibility conditions as the SGST reimbursement

items.name: DPR and machinery transport reimbursement
items.summary: 50% of project report (DPR) cost, max ₹20K micro, ₹50K small, ₹1L medium; 50% of machinery transport.
details: DPR: 50% of consultant charges, max ₹20,000 (micro), ₹50,000 (small) or ₹1 lakh (medium). Inland transport and insurance of plant and machinery: 50%, max ₹2 lakh (A) or ₹3 lakh (B, C).
items.extraFor: Special-category owners, including women: 90% of DPR cost (same caps) and 100% of machinery transport up to ₹3 lakh.
conditions: Same eligibility conditions as the SGST reimbursement

items.name: Mukhya Mantri Swavalamban Yojana (MMSY)
items.summary: Capital subsidy 25% (men) and 30-35% (women) on machinery, plus 5% interest subvention; new cases held for backlog
details: Capital subsidy on plant and machinery: 25% for men, 30-35% for women.
5% interest subvention on the loan; reported project ceiling up to ₹1 crore.
Government land on lease at 1% of rate and stamp duty cut from 6% to 3% (2018 terms).
Aug 2025: minister said the scheme continues but new cases will be taken up after pending subsidy cases are settled.
items.extraFor: Higher capital subsidy for women
conditions: Himachali (bonafide) youth; age limit as per current notification (18 to 35 in the 2018 notification).
Apply online on the MMSY portal through the District Industries Centre.
items.onlyText: Only bonafide Himachali youth

items.name: Startup Himachal incentives (Mukhya Mantri Startup Yojana)
items.summary: Sustenance allowance ₹25,000 a month for one year, seed fund up to ₹50 lakh and patent support up to ₹2 lakh (India) / ₹10 lakh (abroad)
details: Sustenance allowance of ₹25,000 per month for one year, paid directly after empowered committee sanction.
Seed fund of up to ₹50 lakh (HIMSUP Yojana).
Patent filing cost up to ₹2 lakh per Indian and ₹10 lakh per foreign patent.

After commercialisation: 75% of DPR cost (max ₹1 lakh), stamp duty at 3%, land at 50% of department rates in Category B and C areas, and 5% interest subvention for 3 years on loans up to ₹25 lakh for micro units employing at least 5 persons.
conditions: Innovator recommended by a recognised incubation centre in HP.
Apply online on the Startup Himachal portal (Department of Industries); idea approved or rejected within 20 days.
Post-commercialisation benefits are claimed through the state single window portal.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recommended by an HP incubation centre

items.name: Rajiv Gandhi Swarozgar Startup Yojana – e-taxi subsidy
items.summary: 50% subsidy on e-taxi purchase with collateral-free loan; taxi hired by government departments for 5 years
details: E-taxis are attached to state departments and corporations for 5 years (extendable by 2), giving assured monthly income.
Rs 5.64 crore paid to 79 youth by Oct 2025.
conditions: Unemployed Himachal youth above 23 years
Apply online on the HP Transport Department portal; margin money deposit needed for the bank loan
items.onlyText: Only for unemployed youth of Himachal Pradesh above 23 years
apply: HP Transport Department online portal (see launch notice)

items.onlyText: Only for Scheduled Caste applicants (Swarojgar also for Scheduled Tribes)
items.name: HP SC/ST Development Corporation term loans and Swarojgar Yojana
items.summary: NSFDC-funded term loans up to ₹50 lakh at 8% for SC enterprises; small Swarojgar loans with 50% subsidy (max ₹10,000)
details: Term Loan (NSFDC): up to ₹50 lakh at 8%, repayable over 7 years; 80% NSFDC loan, 10% corporation margin money loan, 10% promoter share.
Covers services and transport (tent house, dhaba, light vehicles), small industry (fabrication, furniture) and allied activities.
Swarojgar Yojana: bank loans up to ₹50,000 with 50% capital subsidy up to ₹10,000 and interest of 4% to 6% after interest subsidy on regular repayment.
HIMSWAVLAMBAN (PM-AJAY): NSFDC loans of ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh at 8% with a ₹50,000 back-end capital subsidy for SC applicants.
conditions: Bona fide HP resident from an SC family (Swarojgar also ST); age 18 to 55; not a bank defaulter.
Income limit ₹5 lakh a year for the term loan and ₹50,000 for Swarojgar.
Apply through the corporation's district office or website.

items.name: Chief Minister Tourism Start-up Scheme in Hospitality Industry (Himachal Pradesh)
items.summary: Interest subsidy of 3% (urban), 4% (rural) or 5% (tribal areas) for 3 years on loans up to Rs 2 crore for homestays and tourism units
details: For setting up new tourism units such as homestays, and for upgrading or expanding existing ones.
Interest subsidy of 3% in urban areas, 4% in rural areas and 5% in tribal areas, on loans up to Rs 2 crore, for up to 3 years from loan disbursement.
Approved by the HP Cabinet in September 2025.
items.extraFor: Higher rate (5%) in tribal areas
conditions: Only bona fide Himachali residents
Unit to be registered under the HP Home Stay Rules 2025 or tourism trade rules
Apply through the HP Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation / lending bank
items.onlyText: Only for bona fide residents of Himachal Pradesh
apply: HP Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation

items.name: Himachal Pradesh purchase preference to local micro and small enterprises (Industrial Investment Policy 2019, clause 7(X))
items.summary: State places at least 25% of orders with local MSEs at the lowest approved rate
details: The State Government gives purchase preference to local micro and small enterprises by placing at least 25% of orders with them at the lowest approved rates.
Applies where products meet the required quality and the item is not sophisticated, high-technology or precision in nature.
Startups also get relaxations in prior experience, turnover and EMD in tenders of state departments and PSUs.
conditions: Micro or small enterprise located in Himachal Pradesh with Udyam registration.
Benefit applies in purchases by HP departments; quote in the tender and agree to the lowest approved rate.

states.statusText: In force. Draft amendments and a draft Industrial Policy 2026-35 are not yet notified.

portal.label: J&K Single Window; claims through the District Industries Centre

states.zones: Blocks are Zone A or Zone B (far-flung, higher benefits); the zone changes only the DG-set cap and the land premium.
states.notes: The large capital, interest and GST incentives came from the central J&K scheme (NCSS-2021), which closed registration on 30 Sep 2024. No UT-level extra for women or SC/ST is in force. Artisans and weavers can get loans up to ₹2 lakh with 7% interest subvention under a Credit Card Scheme.

items.name: DG set subsidy
items.summary: 100% subsidy on DG sets (10–2000 KW); max ₹40 lakh in Zone A, ₹45 lakh in Zone B.
details: 100% of purchase and installation cost of DG sets of 10–2000 KW, capped at ₹40 lakh (Zone A) or ₹45 lakh (Zone B). Paid 50% after installation is checked and 50% after six months. Expanding units get subsidy on the added load.
conditions: New units starting commercial production on or after 1 Apr 2021, or existing units doing a substantial expansion
Whether services qualify is unconfirmed

items.name: Stamp duty and court fee exemption
items.summary: 100% exemption of stamp duty and court fee on land transactions in Government Industrial Estates.
details: Full exemption of stamp duty and court fee on land transactions, including lease and mortgage deeds, for land in Government Industrial Estates.
conditions: New units or substantial expansion
Government Industrial Estate land only

items.name: Quality certification and automation subsidy
items.summary: 30% of quality certification cost (max ₹2 lakh); 25% of automation cost (max ₹2 lakh).
details: Quality certification (ISO, ISI, BIS, FPO, BEE, AGMARK, ECOMARK): 30% of cost, one-time max ₹2 lakh. Automation: 25% of cost, max ₹2 lakh, per the UT's Feb 2026 Assembly reply; 2021 press reports said 30%.
conditions: New units, substantial expansion or existing units

items.name: Pollution control device subsidy
items.summary: 60% subsidy on pollution control devices, max ₹50 lakh per unit.
details: 60% of purchase and installation cost of pollution control devices, max ₹50 lakh per unit. Expanding units get only the unused balance of the ₹50 lakh cap. Not available if claimed under another scheme.
conditions: Not combinable with the central capital incentive for the same asset

items.name: Green / environment-friendly technology subsidy
items.summary: 50% subsidy on environment-friendly production technology such as rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling.
details: 50% of spending on environment-friendly production technology such as rainwater harvesting, wastewater recycling, zero-liquid discharge and solid-waste equipment. Cap unconfirmed.
conditions: New units, substantial expansion or existing units

items.name: CGTMSE guarantee-fee reimbursement
items.summary: UT repays the 0.33% annual CGTMSE guarantee fee on loans up to ₹10 lakh.
details: Under G.O. No. 121-JK(IND) of 2025 dated 22 Dec 2025, the UT reimburses the 0.33% annual guarantee fee on loans up to ₹10 lakh covered by existing CGTMSE schemes.
conditions: Loan of ₹10 lakh or less covered by CGTMSE

items.name: Concessional industrial land premium
items.summary: Estate land at concessional premium: ₹5 lakh per kanal (Zone A) or ₹2.5 lakh (Zone B), small plots.
details: Premium per kanal (amended 2024): up to 5 kanal ₹5.0L (A) or ₹2.5L (B); up to 10 kanal ₹6.0L or ₹3.5L; up to 20 kanal ₹7.0L or ₹4.5L; above 20 kanal ₹8.0L or ₹6.0L.
conditions: Allotment under the J&K Industrial Land Allotment Policy 2021-30 (amended 2024)

items.name: Net SGST reimbursement (existing units only)
items.summary: 100% net SGST refunded for 10 years from 1 Apr 2021 to units GST-registered by 31 Mar 2021.
details: Existing units GST-registered in J&K on or before 31 Mar 2021 get 100% net SGST reimbursement for 10 years from 1 Apr 2021, i.e. to 31 Mar 2031.
conditions: Not available to new units
Your GST registration date decides this; it is not on the Udyam certificate

items.name: Local-MSME purchase preference (GeM local filter)
items.summary: UT government buyers use a GeM 'local filter' for purchases up to ₹10 lakh, favouring J&K MSMEs.
details: UT departments apply a local-supplier filter on GeM for purchases up to ₹10 lakh. The UT also supports trade fairs, exhibitions and buyer-seller meets; no fixed rates found.
conditions: Enterprise located in J&K

items.name: Mission YUVA (Nano, focus-sector and existing enterprise support)
items.summary: Nano enterprises: 25% capital subsidy plus 5% interest subvention; focus-sector and existing MSMEs: 6% interest subvention
details: Nano enterprises (typical project ₹5-6 lakh): 25% capital subsidy and 5% interest subvention.
New MSMEs in focus sectors (agri-tech, food processing, renewable energy, tourism, IT) and existing enterprises: 6% interest subvention.
Free DPR support, training and market linkage; ₹594 crore disbursed to over 10,000 entrepreneurs by Jan 2026.
items.extraFor: Focus on women (SHG members), first-generation and remote/border-area youth
conditions: J&K domicile aged 18 to 59.
Register and apply on the Mission YUVA app or portal; bank sanction required.
items.onlyText: Only J&K domiciles aged 18 to 59
apply: Mission YUVA app/portal (via District Employment and Counselling Centre)

items.name: J&K Start-up Policy 2024-27 (seed funding)
items.summary: One-time seed funding up to ₹20 lakh in four instalments for JKEDI-recognised startups, plus a ₹250 crore venture fund
details: Seed funding of up to ₹20 lakh, paid in four equal instalments, to build prototypes, launch products or expand; capped at 25 startups a year.
₹250 crore venture capital fund (UT share up to ₹25 crore) to invest mainly in recognised J&K startups.
Mentorship from national and international experts; help with patent filing through central schemes.
Approved by the J&K Administrative Council in February 2024.
conditions: Startup located in J&K and recognised by JKEDI, the nodal agency.
Selection by a task force committee under the Industries and Commerce Department.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised by JKEDI
apply: JKEDI (nodal agency) via J&K Startup portal

items.name: Tejaswini - The Radiant (Mission Youth J&K)
items.summary: Interest-free loan up to ₹5 lakh for young women, with a 10% (max ₹50,000) special incentive
details: Loan of up to ₹5 lakh through J&K Bank (Mudra), with interest subsidy of up to ₹60,000 so the loan is effectively interest-free.
Special incentive of 10% of project cost or ₹50,000, whichever is lower, adjusted against the first six monthly instalments.
Project cost above ₹5 lakh must be self-financed.
conditions: Woman domicile of J&K aged 18 to 35, Class 10 pass (can be relaxed), unemployed and registered with the District Employment and Counselling Centre.
Individual woman, or an enterprise with at least 50% women holding; not a bank defaulter; once per woman.
Apply online on the Mission Youth portal; a district committee selects within the district quota.
items.onlyText: Only for women of J&K aged 18 to 35

items.name: Karkhandar Scheme (J&K Handicrafts and Handloom)
items.summary: ₹25,000 support to craft units (karkhandars) plus ₹2,000 a month stipend per trainee for 6 months
details: Support to the karkhandar is paid in two instalments for tools, raw material and equipment.
Covers walnut wood carving, silver filigree, Kani and Sozni, papier-mache, khatamband, carpets and copperware.
Phase 1 funds released in Aug 2025 for Anantnag, Budgam, Baramulla, Kulgam and Srinagar; more districts to follow.
conditions: Master craftsmen running a craft unit that trains apprentices in listed crafts
Apply to the Directorate of Handicrafts and Handloom, Kashmir
items.onlyText: Only for master craftsmen (karkhandars) in listed traditional crafts

items.name: J&K Tourism Policy 2020: capital investment subsidy and support for tourism units
items.summary: 15% capital investment subsidy for tourism units in Category B and C areas not covered by the Industrial Policy, plus certification and skilling support
details: 15% of eligible capital investment for new tourism units, or existing units making substantial expansion, in Category B and C areas; ceiling set by the Tourism Department; paid after commercial operations start.
100% reimbursement of eco-tourism certification cost up to Rs 1 lakh (up to 5 units a year).
50% of training cost, up to Rs 10,000 per trainee and Rs 50,000 per unit per programme; 25% of ICT/audio-guide cost up to Rs 2 lakh.
conditions: Covers hotels, resorts, wellness centres, houseboats, adventure and other tourism units, with minimum investment by type (for example wellness unit Rs 1 crore, adventure project Rs 2 crore)
Cannot be combined with J&K Industrial Policy incentives for the same unit
Policy valid 10 years from 2020; apply to J&K Tourism Department

states.short: Draft Jharkhand Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy 2026
states.statusText: Not in force. The 2026 policy is still a draft, and no extension of the 2021 policy was found.

portal.label: Jharkhand single window

states.notes: A separate draft Textile, Apparel and Footwear Policy 2026 reportedly offers a 20% capital subsidy.

items.name: Capital subsidy (draft JIIPP 2026)
items.summary: Draft: 20% of fixed capital investment, capped at ₹15 crore, for MSMEs.
details: Draft only. Non-MSME units: 25% up to ₹30 crore. SC, ST, women and differently-abled entrepreneurs: additional 5%.
items.extraFor: SC, ST, women, differently-abled: additional 5% (draft)
conditions: Not notified - do not show as available
Expansion eligibility unconfirmed

items.name: SGST reimbursement (draft JIIPP 2026)
items.summary: Draft: 100% SGST reimbursement for seven years, then 40% for three years.
details: Draft only; caps and eligibility unconfirmed.
conditions: Not notified - do not show as available

items.name: Stamp duty and registration reimbursement (draft JIIPP 2026)
items.summary: Draft: full reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges.
details: Draft only; scope (land, lease or loan deeds) unconfirmed.
conditions: Not notified - do not show as available

items.name: Electricity tariff and duty reimbursement (draft JIIPP 2026)
items.summary: Draft: electricity tariff and electricity-tax reimbursement; rates unconfirmed.
details: Draft only; percentages and duration unconfirmed.
conditions: Not notified - do not show as available

items.name: Wage and training support (draft JIIPP 2026)
items.summary: Draft: wage support ₹5,000 a month per male and ₹6,000 per female employee.
details: Draft only; duration, caps and domicile conditions unconfirmed. Training assistance up to ₹13,000 per trainee.
items.extraFor: Women employees: ₹6,000/month vs ₹5,000 (draft)
conditions: Not notified - do not show as available

items.name: Mukhyamantri Rojgar Srijan Yojana (CMEGP Jharkhand)
items.summary: Loan for self-employment with 40% subsidy (up to ₹5 lakh) at about 6% interest for ST, SC, minority, BC and PwD youth
details: Subsidy of 40% of the loan or ₹5 lakh, whichever is lower; EMI is worked out on the balance after subsidy.
Loans reported up to ₹25 lakh; interest about 6%; no guarantor for loans up to ₹50,000; entrepreneurship training before start.
Run by the Department of ST, SC, Minority and Backward Class Welfare through the state Tribal, SC, Backward Class and Minority finance corporations.
conditions: Permanent resident of Jharkhand from ST, SC, minority or backward class, or a person with 40%+ disability; age 18 to 50; family income up to ₹5 lakh a year.
Not in a government job and not a bank defaulter; above ₹50,000 a 10% margin and guarantor or collateral are needed.
Apply through the district welfare office or the relevant state finance corporation.
items.onlyText: Only for ST, SC, minority, backward class and disabled entrepreneurs of Jharkhand
apply: District Welfare Office / state welfare finance corporation

items.name: Jharkhand Startup Policy 2023
items.summary: Grants for startups: stipend, 50% rent (up to ₹5 lakh a year), patent cost reimbursement, marketing grant up to ₹10 lakh
details: Approved by the state cabinet on 7 Dec 2023 for five years (to 2028); implemented by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Innovation Lab (ABVIL), which opened online applications from 4 Feb 2025.

Listed incentives include full reimbursement of patent filing costs, 50% lease rent reimbursement in STPIs, IT parks or SEZs (up to ₹5 lakh a year), utility bill support, a founder stipend and a one-time marketing grant of up to ₹10 lakh.
conditions: Startup registered in Jharkhand, under 5 years old, turnover under ₹25 crore, selected by the State Evaluation Board.
Apply online through ABVIL.
items.onlyText: Only for startups selected under the Jharkhand Startup Policy

items.name: Jharkhand State Industrial Procurement Policy (preference to state MSEs)
items.summary: 20% of state purchases from Jharkhand MSEs, price preference up to 15%, and 31 products reserved for them
details: Government departments, aided institutions and state enterprises must buy 20% of annual purchases from Jharkhand MSEs.
Price preference of up to 15% for state MSEs.
31 products are reserved for purchase from state MSEs.
conditions: Micro or small unit located in Jharkhand with Udyam registration.
Check the current reserved list and preference terms with the Directorate of Industries before bidding.

items.name: Draft Jharkhand Textile, Apparel and Footwear Policy 2026
items.summary: Draft: 20% investment subsidy (up to 35% with add-ons), 50% power tariff and 100% SGST reimbursement, wage aid
details: Draft released for comments in July 2026; not yet notified.
20% Comprehensive Project Investment Subsidy on fixed capital investment, capped at ₹50 crore; add-ons can raise it to 35%.
50% power tariff reimbursement and 100% electricity duty reimbursement for 5 years (7 years with renewable energy).
100% net SGST reimbursement for 7 years, then 40% for 3 years; wage support up to ₹6,000 per worker per month.
conditions: Textile, apparel and footwear units in Jharkhand.
Final terms will apply only after Cabinet approval and notification; draft is on the Jharkhand Single Window portal.

states.statusText: In force. Operative guidelines for the incentive package were approved on 10 Apr 2026.

portal.label: Karnataka Udyog Mitra single window; claims go to the Joint Director of the DIC

states.zones: Taluks are Zone 1 (199 taluks, highest rates), Zone 2 (32) or Zone 3 (Bengaluru Urban and Rural; incentives only in Bengaluru Rural). Most-backward and more-backward taluks get 5% or 3% extra.
states.notes: The guidelines use older size limits (plant and machinery under ₹1 crore micro, ₹1–10 crore small, ₹10–50 crore medium), so your state category can differ from Udyam. Most MSME rates come from a consultancy summary of the guidelines.

items.name: Capital subsidy – micro and small
items.summary: Micro: 30% of fixed-asset value up to ₹30 lakh (Zone 1); small: 25% up to ₹2 crore.
details: Micro: Z1 30% ≤₹30L (special category 35% ≤₹35L); Z2 25% ≤₹25L (30% ≤₹30L); Z3 Bengaluru Rural 10% (special 15% ≤₹15L). Small: Z1 25% ≤₹2 Cr (30% ≤₹2.25 Cr); Z2 20% ≤₹1.5 Cr (25% ≤₹1.75 Cr); Z3 10% ≤₹50L (15% ≤₹75L). Paid in 2 annual instalments.
items.extraFor: Special category (units wholly owned by SC/ST, women, minorities, physically challenged or ex-servicemen): 5 points more and higher caps
conditions: Manufacturing plus 20 listed service activities (e.g., testing labs, powder coating, recycling); no trading
New investment from 2025-02-08, or expansion/diversification/modernisation adding ≥25% to fixed assets
Production within 3 years of approval; apply within 1 year of production
70% Kannadiga employment (100% for Group D)
29-item negative list (e.g., breweries, tobacco, sawmills, hotels, laundries)

items.name: Medium enterprises: capex base subsidy or PLI
items.summary: Medium: 25% of fixed-asset value up to ₹10 crore (Zone 1), or a turnover-linked PLI of 2.5%.
details: Capex: Z1 25% ≤₹10 Cr; Z2 20% ≤₹8 Cr; Z3 10% ≤₹4 Cr. PLI alternative: Z1 2.5%, Z2 2.0% of net sales turnover (cap 60% of fixed-asset value); Z3 1.0% (cap 30%). Choice fixed at application; capex paid in 4 instalments.
conditions: Turnover-based incentives exclude trading and resales

items.name: Backward-taluk top-up
items.summary: Extra 5% (most backward taluks) or 3% (more backward taluks) capital subsidy.
conditions: Taluk status per the Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa Committee

items.name: Stamp duty reimbursement and concessional registration
items.summary: 100% stamp duty reimbursement on land and loan documents (Zones 1-2); registration at ₹1 per ₹1,000.
details: Reimbursed instead of exempted, for lease, lease-cum-sale and sale deeds and loan documents. Zone 3: 75% for special category only (secondary source).
items.extraFor: Zone 3: special category only

items.name: Land conversion fee reimbursement
items.summary: 100% of the land conversion fee reimbursed after commercial production (Zones 1-2).
details: Zone 3: 75% for special category only (secondary source).
items.extraFor: Zone 3: special category only
conditions: Claim after commercial production

items.name: Exemption from tax on electricity
items.summary: 100% electricity tax exemption for 7 years in Zone 1 (8 years for special category).
details: Zone 2: 100% (years unconfirmed). Zone 3: 75% for special category only. The guidelines say it awaits an enabling Energy Department notification.
items.extraFor: Special category: 1 extra year in Zone 1
conditions: Pending Energy Department notification

items.name: Power subsidy (micro and small)
items.summary: ₹1 per unit power cost reimbursement for 3 years (Zones 1-2).
details: Not available in Zone 3.

items.name: Quality and export certification support
items.summary: 50% of cost, up to ₹5 lakh each, for quality certification and export certification.
details: All zones.

items.name: Udyogini Scheme (Karnataka State Women's Development Corporation)
items.summary: Bank loan up to ₹3 lakh for women's small businesses with KSWDC subsidy (rate depends on category; not confirmed)
details: KSWDC provides subsidy; banks sanction loans; entrepreneurship training before disbursement.
2024-25 budget ₹15 crore for about 1,540 women.
items.extraFor: Higher subsidy for SC/ST women
conditions: Women resident in Karnataka within the income and age limits set in current guidelines.
Apply through the district Women and Child Development office / KSWDC.
items.onlyText: Only for women entrepreneurs

items.name: ELEVATE startup grant (incl. Elevate Unnati and Elevate Minorities)
items.summary: One-time grant up to ₹50 lakh for prototypes, proof of concept and scaling; 146 startups got ₹38.85 crore in Jan 2026
details: Run by Karnataka's Department of Electronics, IT, Bt and S&T (Startup Karnataka) through periodic calls.
Elevate Unnati (SC/ST-led) and Elevate Minorities are separate calls.
items.extraFor: Separate Elevate Unnati calls for SC/ST founders and Elevate Minorities
conditions: Startup registered in Karnataka (Karnataka startup recognition).
Apply online when a call opens.

items.name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Development Corporation self-employment schemes
items.summary: Bank-linked self-employment: 50% subsidy (max ₹35,000) for units under ₹1 lakh; 33% (max ₹2 lakh) for units of ₹1 lakh and above
details: ISB programme: 33% subsidy, 62% bank loan, 5% own contribution.
Also dairy units (50% subsidy up to ₹50,000) and SHG micro-finance.
conditions: Scheduled Caste, Karnataka resident 15 years, aged 18 to 60, no family member in government service, within the corporation's income limit.
Beneficiaries selected by a committee; apply at the district/taluk office of the corporation.
items.onlyText: Only for Scheduled Caste applicants
apply: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Development Corporation (district office)

items.name: KSFC Interest Subsidy Scheme for SC/ST Entrepreneurs (4% effective rate)
items.summary: KSFC loans of ₹20 lakh to ₹10 crore at an effective 4% interest; state pays the rest
details: Includes one-time working capital term loan up to ₹50 lakh.
Repayment 8 years (loans up to ₹5 crore) or up to 10 years (above ₹5 crore).
conditions: Unit fully owned by SC/ST promoters; micro, small or service enterprise; no other interest subsidy taken.
Apply at a KSFC branch office.
items.onlyText: Only for units wholly owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs

items.name: KSFC Interest Subvention Scheme for MSEs (5.5%)
items.summary: 5.5% a year interest subvention for 5 years on KSFC term loans up to ₹5 crore for building and machinery
details: Loans ₹5 lakh up to ₹5 crore (manufacturing MSEs) or ₹2 crore (manufacturing-allied services); amount above the limit at contract rate.
conditions: Any constitution; new investment in building, plant and machinery; trading, land purchase and refinancing excluded.
Regular repayment required; apply at a KSFC branch.

items.name: Karnataka Tourism Policy 2024-29: tourism project incentives
items.summary: Capital or interest subsidy for listed tourism projects, stamp duty and registration exemption, and industrial power rates (subsidy rates not confirmed)
details: Stamp duty and registration charges exempted on land and loan documents for approved tourism projects.
Projects with industry status pay electricity, water and property tax at industrial rates.

Capital investment subsidy for adventure and agri tourism, caravan parks, convention/MICE centres, budget and premium hotels, houseboats, wellness centres and wayside amenities; interest subsidy for heritage hotels, cultural villages, museums and sound-and-light shows; separate concessions for homestays.
Subsidy percentages and caps are set in the department's guidelines (amount not confirmed).
conditions: Apply online on karnatakatourism.org; projects up to Rs 5 crore are approved by the District Tourism Committee, larger ones by the State Empowered Committee.
Complete the project within the approved timeline and register under the KTTF Act 2015.

items.name: Karnataka Textile and Apparel Policy (4.0) 2026-31
items.summary: New textile policy (Rs 4,000 crore outlay) notified 30 Sep 2026; extra incentives in 34 focused taluks and PM MITRA Park Kalaburagi (rates not confirmed)
details: Notified 30 Sep 2026 and valid for five years; follows the 2019-24 textile and garment policy.
Additional incentives and concessions for eligible new units in 34 focused taluks, special provisions for Kalyana Karnataka and for units in the PM MITRA Park, Kalaburagi.
Covers silk reeling and spinning for the first time, plus technical textiles, exports, skilling and sustainable manufacturing.
Unit-level subsidy rates and caps: amount not confirmed.
conditions: Textile, apparel and silk-yarn units in Karnataka.
Apply to the Department of Handlooms and Textiles, Karnataka, once operational guidelines are issued.
apply: Department of Handlooms and Textiles, Karnataka

items.onlyText: Only for Backward Class applicants in Karnataka
items.name: D. Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation self-employment schemes
items.summary: Chaitanya subsidy-cum-soft loan and direct loans at 4% for Backward Class self-employment
details: Chaitanya Subsidy cum Soft Loan: bank loan for units up to ₹5 lakh with 20% margin money from the corporation at 4%, plus subsidy up to ₹10,000.
Chaitanya Direct Loan up to ₹50,000 at 4% with 30% subsidy (max ₹10,000); micro credit, artisan and occupational group loans also offered.
NBCFDC-funded term loans (Term Loan, Mahila Samrudhi, Shilpa Sampada and others) are also routed through the corporation.
conditions: Backward Class applicant resident in Karnataka.
Apply at the corporation's district office.

items.onlyText: Only for religious minority applicants in Karnataka
items.name: KMDC Shramashakthi and Swavalambana loans (Karnataka Minorities Development Corporation)
items.summary: Loans up to ₹50,000 for minority artisans with 50% back-end subsidy; bank-linked business loans under Swavalambana
details: Shramashakthi: up to ₹50,000 at a low interest rate, half treated as back-end subsidy, for artisans starting or growing a small business.
Swavalambana: bank-linked support for minority persons starting or improving a business, small industry, service or agri activity (amount not confirmed).
Micro Loan with Subsidy for minority SHGs of 10 to 20 members, with priority to women's groups.
conditions: Member of a religious minority resident in Karnataka.
Apply on the KMDC website or at its district office.

items.name: Weavers Special Package: powerlooms, electronic jacquard and knotting machine subsidy (Karnataka)
items.summary: 50% subsidy (90% for SC/ST) on 2 powerlooms (Rs 3 lakh unit), electronic jacquard (Rs 4.5 lakh) or knotting machine (Rs 5 lakh)
details: Maximum subsidy: Rs 1.5 lakh on powerlooms, Rs 2.25 lakh on electronic jacquard, Rs 2.5 lakh on knotting machine for general category.
Group schemes also cover common facility centres (Rs 10 to 15 lakh), mini powerloom parks, sizing and processing plants for SPVs of weavers.
items.extraFor: SC/ST weavers get 90% subsidy (up to Rs 2.7 to 4.5 lakh)
conditions: For weavers setting up their own powerloom unit; balance cost from own funds or bank loan.
Apply through the Deputy Director of Handlooms and Textiles of the district.
items.onlyText: Only for powerloom weavers
apply: Karnataka Department of Handlooms and Textiles

items.name: Free and concessional power for weavers (Karnataka)
items.summary: Free power up to 250 units/month for small weavers with connections below 10 HP; Rs 1.25/unit tariff for 1 to 20 HP pre-loom and powerloom units
details: State cabinet approved free power up to 250 units a month for small and marginal weavers using looms and pre-looms (August 2023).
The department also bears the difference between the actual tariff and Rs 1.25 per unit for powerloom and pre-loom units with 1 to 20 HP connections.
conditions: Loom or pre-loom power connection below 10 HP for free units; 1 to 20 HP for concessional tariff.
Register through the Department of Handlooms and Textiles and the ESCOM.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom, powerloom and pre-loom weavers
apply: Karnataka Department of Handlooms and Textiles

items.name: Kaimagga Vikasa Yojane and Pneumatic/Motorised Jacquard Kit scheme (Karnataka handlooms)
items.summary: 50% assistance on new handlooms (75% for co-op societies); 75% grant (90% SC/ST) on pneumatic or motorised jacquard kits
details: Kaimagga Vikasa Yojane helps weavers buy cotton, silk or woollen handlooms.
Jacquard kit scheme reduces strain and raises output of existing handloom weavers.
items.extraFor: SC/ST weavers get 90% on jacquard kits
conditions: Handloom weavers in Karnataka; co-operative societies for the 75% loom rate.
Apply through the district Deputy Director of Handlooms and Textiles.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom weavers and weavers' co-operative societies
apply: Karnataka Department of Handlooms and Textiles

items.name: Interest subsidy on loans to handloom weavers (Karnataka)
items.summary: Co-operative loans up to Rs 2 lakh at 1% interest; 3% interest subsidy on loans of Rs 2 to 5 lakh
details: Applies to weavers borrowing from co-operative and urban co-operative banks.
Primary weavers' co-operative societies also get 3% interest reimbursement on NABARD refinance cash-credit limits.
conditions: Handloom weaver in Karnataka borrowing from a co-operative bank.
Apply through the lending co-operative bank or district Handlooms and Textiles office.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom weavers
apply: Karnataka Department of Handlooms and Textiles

items.name: Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025-30: capital subsidy for EV and clean-mobility manufacturing
items.summary: Capital subsidy up to 25% of capital expenditure for clean-mobility projects (20% in Bengaluru Urban and Rural)
details: Covers EV, battery and component manufacturing across the clean-mobility value chain.
Capital subsidy up to 25% on capital expenditure; 20% in Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru Rural districts.
Effective 11 Feb 2025 for five years; MSME-specific slabs not confirmed.
conditions: Apply through Karnataka Udyog Mitra / Department of Industries and Commerce
apply: Department of Industries and Commerce, Karnataka

items.name: Karnataka public procurement relaxations for startups
items.summary: EMD waived and prior turnover/experience criteria relaxed for startups in Karnataka tenders
details: Prior turnover and prior experience criteria relaxed for startups (G.O. FD 218 Exp-12/2021, 1 Sep 2021).
EMD submission waived for startups (G.O. ITD 27 PRM 2015, 16 Sep 2017).
conditions: Startup recognised under the Karnataka Startup Policy.
Claim the relaxation in the bid on the Karnataka e-procurement portal.

items.name: Karnataka Startup Policy 2025-30 (with 2022-27 incentives)
items.summary: Rs 518 crore policy approved 6 Nov 2025; marketing support up to Rs 5 lakh/yr, patent up to Rs 2 lakh (Indian)
details: Policy approved by cabinet on 6 Nov 2025 with Rs 518.27 crore over five years, targeting 25,000 startups, with a Beyond Bengaluru cluster seed fund and the Elevate NxT deep-tech programme.

Incentives under the 2022-27 policy: marketing cost support up to 30% or Rs 5 lakh a year; patent cost up to Rs 2 lakh per Indian and Rs 10 lakh per foreign patent; 50% of quality certification cost up to Rs 6 lakh.
100% SGST reimbursement for up to 3 years for eligible startups in government incubators outside Bengaluru.
Detailed 2025-30 incentive amounts not confirmed.
items.extraFor: At least 10% of seats in government-supported incubators are kept for startups with women co-founders.
conditions: Startup recognised under the Karnataka Startup Policy.
Apply through the Karnataka Startup Cell portal.

states.short: Kerala Industrial Policy 2023 and the Entrepreneur Support Scheme
states.period: ESS running; rates as on the Industries Department site
states.statusText: In force.

portal.label: ESS portal, Directorate of Industries and Commerce

states.zones: Idukki, Wayanad, Kasaragod and Pathanamthitta get 10% more under ESS.
states.notes: ESS covers manufacturing only. KELS, the nano-unit schemes and MSME insurance have their own portals, linked on each item.

items.name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme (ESS) - investment support
items.summary: Investment subsidy 15% (max ₹30 lakh); 25% (max ₹40 lakh) for young, women, SC/ST, NRK entrepreneurs.
details: On land, building, plant & machinery, electrification, office equipment, pollution-control devices. Extra 10% (max ₹10 lakh each) for priority sectors, units in Idukki/Wayanad/Kasaragod/Pathanamthitta, or technology from approved institutions; overall ceiling ₹40 lakh. Start-up support: up to 50% of eligible aid (max ₹3 lakh) on term-loan sanction.
items.extraFor: Young (18-45), women, SC/ST, Non-Resident Keralite entrepreneurs: 25%, cap ₹40 lakh
conditions: Manufacturing only; services excluded
Apply within 1 year of commercial production (technology support within 6 months)
Must run 5 years continuously
Expansion/diversification/modernisation: incremental investment only
Not on negative list

items.name: Kerala Entrepreneur Loan Scheme (KELS)
items.summary: Interest subvention so that loans up to ₹10 lakh cost 4% for the first five years.
details: Term and working-capital loans; subvention for the first 5 years or until closure, whichever is earlier; enterprises established after 1-Apr-2022 (Udyam date); new units and expansions.
conditions: Enterprise established on or after 2022-04-01
Apply via kels.industry.kerala.gov.in

items.name: Margin Money Grant to Nano Units
items.summary: Margin money grant 30% (max ₹3 lakh), or 40% (max ₹4 lakh) for special categories.
details: New nano proprietary units with project cost up to ₹10 lakh (fixed plus working capital); bank loan at least 40%; own contribution at least 30% (20% for special categories). 30% of beneficiaries reserved for women.
items.extraFor: Women, youth (18-40), differently-abled, ex-servicemen, SC/ST: 40%, cap ₹4 lakh
conditions: New nano proprietary unit
Project cost up to ₹10 lakh

items.name: Interest Subvention Scheme for Nano Household Units
items.summary: Term-loan interest subvention 6% a year (8% for women, SC/ST) for three years.
details: Nano/household units with fixed investment up to ₹10 lakh (excluding land and building), connected load up to 5 HP, white/green category; subvention lost for any year with repayment default.
items.extraFor: Women and SC/ST enterprises: 8% a year
conditions: Not for units covered by ESS or other concessional schemes

items.name: MSME Insurance Scheme
items.summary: 50% of annual MSME insurance premium reimbursed, up to ₹2,500 per unit a year.
details: Bharat Sookshma/Laghu Udyam policies from National, United India, Oriental or New India Assurance; policy period after 1-Apr-2023; claim through the District Industries Centre.
conditions: Udyam registration in Kerala

items.name: MSME Scale-Up Mission (Mission 1000)
items.summary: Selected scale-up MSMEs: capital subsidy up to 40% (max ₹2 crore) and 50% working-capital interest subvention.
details: Working-capital interest subvention up to 50%, max ₹50 lakh; DPR aid up to ₹1 lakh; handholding. Competitive selection of 1,000 units in operation for at least 3 years as of 31-Mar-2023; trading excluded. Current selection round unconfirmed.
conditions: Selected by scoring (turnover, profit, exports, jobs, CIBIL)
Apply via mission1000.industry.kerala.gov.in

items.name: Stamp duty and registration waiver (Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: Up to 100% stamp duty/registration waiver for manufacturing units in government or notified private industrial parks.
details: Women, SC/ST and transgender entrepreneurs: waiver anywhere in the state. Stated in Industrial Policy 2023; implementing G.O. not confirmed.
items.extraFor: Women, SC/ST, transgender entrepreneurs: anywhere in Kerala
conditions: Implementation G.O. unconfirmed - verify before showing

items.name: Electricity duty exemption (Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: Policy 2023 promises 100% electricity duty exemption for five years to MSMEs.
details: Implementing notification not confirmed; treat as unverified.
conditions: Implementation unconfirmed - verify before showing

items.name: KESRU (Kerala State Self Employment Scheme for the Registered Unemployed)
items.summary: Bank loan up to ₹1 lakh for registered unemployed, with 20% of the loan as government subsidy; no collateral
details: Loan up to ₹1 lakh from nationalised, scheduled or district co-operative banks or KSFE; 20% of the loan reimbursed as subsidy by the Employment Department.
No beneficiary contribution or collateral; a spouse or parent stands guarantor.
items.extraFor: Preference for professionally or technically qualified applicants, graduate women and those on unemployment allowance.
conditions: Registered and active with an Employment Exchange, aged 21 to 50, annual family income up to ₹1 lakh; students not eligible.
Apply at the Employment Exchange where registered with a project report and income certificate; sanction by the District Committee.
items.onlyText: Only for unemployed people aged 21 to 50 registered with an Employment Exchange, family income up to ₹1 lakh

items.name: Saranya self-employment scheme (Kerala Employment Department)
items.summary: Interest-free loan up to Rs 50,000 with 50% subsidy (max Rs 25,000) for destitute and single women
details: Loan repaid in 60 monthly instalments, no security needed; above Rs 50,000 the beneficiary adds 10% and pays 3% flat interest on the excess.
A successful venture that repaid at least 50% can get a further loan of up to 80% of the original amount.
Joint ventures allowed, each member getting the full loan and subsidy.
conditions: Unemployed widows, divorced or deserted women, unmarried women over 30 and ST unwed mothers registered with an Employment Exchange; age 18 to 55 (no upper limit for unmarried women).
Annual family income up to Rs 1 lakh.
Apply at the Employment Exchange where registered, with a project report and Village Officer income certificate.
items.onlyText: Only for widowed, divorced, deserted or unmarried women (and ST unwed mothers) on the Employment Exchange register

items.name: Navajeevan self-employment scheme for job seekers aged 50 to 65
items.summary: Bank loan for a self-employment venture with 25% subsidy (max Rs 12,500) for registered job seekers aged 50 to 65
details: Run by the Kerala Employment Department through Employment Exchanges.
Loans come from nationalised, scheduled and co-operative banks, KSFE and other institutions; the department pays the subsidy.
conditions: Age 50 to 65 and on the live register of an Employment Exchange.
Personal annual income up to Rs 1 lakh.
Apply at the local Employment Exchange.
items.onlyText: Only for Employment Exchange registrants aged 50 to 65

items.name: KSUM Innovation Grants (Idea, Productisation, Market Acceleration and Scale-up grants)
items.summary: Kerala Startup Mission grants: idea up to Rs 3 lakh, productisation up to Rs 7 lakh, market acceleration up to Rs 10 lakh, scale-up up to Rs 15 lakh
details: Grants form a ladder; a startup can claim the balance under later stages.
Separate productisation grant up to Rs 5 lakh for women- or transgender-led startups.
Market acceleration grant is milestone-based with a 30% margin contribution; scale-up needs Rs 10 lakh revenue in 6 months or Rs 30 lakh external equity.
items.extraFor: Separate productisation grant (up to Rs 5 lakh) for women- or transgender-led startups
conditions: Kerala startup with a KSUM Unique ID.
Apply on the KSUM Innovation Grant portal during calls; selection by expert panel.
items.onlyText: Only for startups registered with Kerala Startup Mission

items.name: KSIDC WE Funding (Women Entrepreneur loan)
items.summary: KSIDC term loan up to 80% of project cost (max Rs 50 lakh) at 7.5% floating for women-owned units, with 2% interest subsidy
details: For expansion, modernisation or diversification of existing women-led manufacturing or service units using industrial machinery.
Tenure up to 6 years including up to 6 months moratorium; relaxed collateral; mentoring and training are mandatory.
conditions: Women hold at least 51% and manage the firm (proprietorship, partnership, LLP or private limited).
Average turnover of at least Rs 10 lakh over the last 3 years for loans up to Rs 25 lakh; larger loans need last-year turnover of at least twice the loan.
Apply to KSIDC with its application form.
items.onlyText: Only for existing firms at least 51% owned and managed by women

items.name: KSIDC Scale Up Funding for startups
items.summary: KSIDC loan up to Rs 1 crore (70% of project cost) at 7% simple floating interest for revenue-stage Kerala startups
details: Tenure 4 years including a 1-year moratorium.
Collateral-free up to Rs 50 lakh (personal guarantee and primary security); above that, collateral of at least 50% of the loan.
conditions: Private limited company with KSUM or DPIIT registration that has a product and revenue, or has used seed assistance well, has major recognition or external investment.
Promoter must bring and spend at least 30% of the project cost before the first tranche.
Apply to KSIDC.
items.onlyText: Only for KSUM- or DPIIT-registered private limited startups

items.name: Kerala Logistics Park Policy 2024
items.summary: Capital subsidy up to Rs 7 crore for a logistics park (10+ acres) and Rs 3 crore for a mini logistics park (5+ acres), plus stamp duty waiver
details: Investment subsidy up to Rs 7 crore for logistics parks of at least 10 acres and up to Rs 3 crore for mini logistics parks of at least 5 acres.
Stamp duty and registration fees waived on purchase or lease of land for the park.
Approved by the Kerala Cabinet on 4 Sep 2024; parks can be private or PPP.
conditions: Private developer or PPP setting up a logistics park in Kerala that meets the minimum land size.
Apply to the Department of Industries and Commerce, Kerala.
apply: Department of Industries and Commerce, Kerala

items.name: Chief Minister's Entrepreneurship Development Programme (CMEDP), Kerala Financial Corporation
items.summary: KFC loans up to ₹5 crore at 6% (3% state subvention plus 2% KFC rebate) for new and existing MSMEs
details: Edition III launched 6 Aug 2026: loan cap raised from ₹2 crore to ₹5 crore; moratorium up to one year.
Age limit for the main promoter raised from 50 to 60 years.
Interest support covers the first five years; KFC also gives training and follow-up support.
conditions: Udyam-registered MSME in Kerala; new ventures, expansion or modernisation.
Apply online at kfc.org; KFC appraises the project.

items.onlyText: Only for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe applicants
items.name: KSDC loans for SC/ST start-up entrepreneurs and multi-purpose units
items.summary: Loans up to ₹50 lakh at 6% (up to ₹5 lakh) and 8% above, for SC/ST enterprises
details: Kerala State Development Corporation for SC/ST: Loan for Startup Entrepreneurs (SC, up to ₹50 lakh, family income up to ₹25 lakh).
Multi Purpose Unit Loan up to ₹50 lakh (SC/ST, income up to ₹5 lakh); Laghu Vyavasay Yojana ₹4 lakh at 6%; Professional Service Scheme up to ₹5 lakh at 7%.
Beneficiary Oriented Scheme up to ₹3 lakh at 6% for unemployed SC/ST; repayment usually 5 years.
conditions: SC/ST applicant aged 18 to 55 (limits vary by scheme).
Apply at the KSDC district office.

items.onlyText: Only for women entrepreneurs (some lines limited to SC, ST, OBC or minority women)
items.name: KSWDC self-employment loans for women
items.summary: Women's self-employment loans of ₹5 lakh at 8%, plus NBCFDC/NMDFC/NSFDC-funded loans up to ₹45 lakh
details: KSWDC General Scheme: ₹5 lakh at 8%, family income up to ₹8 lakh, age 18 to 60, 5-year repayment.
Channelled loans: minorities up to ₹30 lakh at 6%; backward classes up to ₹25 lakh at 8%; SC up to ₹45 lakh at 8%; ST women up to ₹2 lakh at 4%.
NORKA Vanitha Mithra: up to ₹30 lakh for women returned emigrants, 15% capital subsidy (max ₹3 lakh) and 3% interest subsidy for 4 years.
conditions: Woman resident of Kerala; income limits vary by scheme.
Apply to Kerala State Women's Development Corporation.

items.onlyText: Only for agro-based and food processing MSMEs
items.name: KFC Agro-based MSME Loan Scheme (KAMS)
items.summary: Term and working capital loans for agro-based MSMEs at an effective 6% (3% state subvention plus 2% prompt-repayment rebate)
details: State subvention of 3% on combined loans up to ₹10 crore for the first 5 years; KFC gives a further 2% rebate for prompt repayment.
Covers agro, dairy and animal husbandry units, food processing, warehouses and cold storages, agri-infrastructure and agro-product trading; moratorium up to 2 years, repayment up to 10 years.
conditions: Udyam registration; minimum 10% promoter contribution and KFC internal rating of at least 40%.
Apply online at kfc.org.

items.onlyText: Only for KSUM and DPIIT-registered startups
items.name: Startup Kerala loan scheme (Kerala Financial Corporation)
items.summary: Startup loans from 6.6%: up to ₹25 lakh (productisation), ₹50 lakh (commercialisation), ₹2 crore (scale-up)
details: Collateral-free financing up to ₹10 crore in total across stages; moratorium up to 1 year, repayment up to 5 years.
Promoter contribution at least 10% of project cost.
conditions: Registered with Kerala Startup Mission and DPIIT, with office and operations in Kerala; Indian promoters hold at least 51%.
Apply online at kfc.org.

items.name: NORKA Vanitha Mithra loan scheme (returned women emigrants)
items.summary: Loans up to Rs 30 lakh for women returning from abroad, 3% interest subsidy for 4 years and up to Rs 3 lakh capital subsidy
details: Run by KSWDC with NORKA Roots.
Loan up to Rs 30 lakh; 3% interest subsidy for the first four years.
Capital subsidy of 15% of project cost, up to Rs 3 lakh, for regular repayment.
conditions: Woman who worked or stayed abroad for at least two years and has returned to Kerala.
Apply to KSWDC; sanction after NORKA Roots approval.
items.onlyText: Only for women returned from employment abroad (at least two years)

items.name: Women-friendly tourism enterprise loan (Responsible Tourism Mission and KSWDC)
items.summary: Special 4% interest loans for women starting tourism businesses under Kerala's women-friendly tourism initiative
details: Announced 6 Aug 2025 by the Tourism Department; Rs 4 crore earmarked.
Loans at 4% interest via KSWDC for women registered under the women-friendly tourism initiative, across 24 tourism-linked sectors.
Loan limits not confirmed; announced as launching soon.
conditions: Woman registered with the Responsible Tourism Mission's women-friendly tourism initiative.
Apply through RT Mission or KSWDC once applications open.
items.onlyText: Only for women registered under the women-friendly tourism initiative

items.name: KSMDFC self-employment loans for minorities
items.summary: Kerala Minorities Development Finance Corporation loans up to Rs 30 lakh at 6% for women (8% men)
details: Credit Line 1: up to Rs 20 lakh at 6% for low-income families.
Credit Line 2: up to Rs 30 lakh at 6% for women and 8% for men, family income below Rs 6 lakh.
KSMDFC's own scheme: up to Rs 20 lakh at 8%; Business Development Loan up to Rs 5 lakh; Pravasi loan up to Rs 10 lakh at 5% for returned expatriates.
Loan covers up to 95% of project cost.
items.extraFor: Lower 6% rate for women under Credit Line 2.
conditions: Member of a minority community in Kerala, aged about 18 to 56.
Apply at KSMDFC head or regional offices.
items.onlyText: Only for members of minority communities

items.name: Trade fair participation support (Kerala Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: 100% of stall charges reimbursed, up to ₹5 lakh, for one domestic and one international fair a year
details: Reimbursement of up to 100% of stall charges, capped at ₹5 lakh.
Covers one domestic and one international trade fair or exhibition per year.
conditions: Enterprise must be located in Kerala.
Apply to the Department of Industries and Commerce (District Industries Centre) or KSIDC with fair invoices and proof of participation.
apply: Kerala Department of Industries and Commerce / KSIDC

items.name: Intellectual property support (Kerala Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: 50% of patent, copyright, trademark and GI registration costs, up to ₹30 lakh
details: Reimbursement of 50% of expenses on patents, copyrights, trademarks, GI registration and similar IP.
Maximum ₹30 lakh.
conditions: Enterprise must be located in Kerala.
Apply to the Department of Industries and Commerce or KSIDC with IP filing receipts.
apply: Kerala Department of Industries and Commerce / KSIDC

items.name: Quality certification support (Kerala Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: 50% of certification costs (CE, FDA, ISO, BIS etc.), up to ₹25 lakh per unit per year
details: Reimbursement of 50% of the cost of quality certifications such as CE, FDA, ISO and BIS.
Maximum ₹25 lakh per unit per year.
conditions: Enterprise must be located in Kerala.
Apply with certification and payment documents to the Department of Industries and Commerce or KSIDC.
apply: Kerala Department of Industries and Commerce / KSIDC

items.name: Industry 4.0, R&D and sustainability support (Kerala Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: 20% of Industry 4.0 costs (up to ₹25 lakh), 20% of R&D with Kerala universities (up to ₹1 crore), 25% of green equipment
details: Industry 4.0: 20% of software (for example big data tools) and machinery costs, up to ₹25 lakh per unit over the policy period.
R&D: 20% of R&D costs for units working with universities in Kerala, up to ₹1 crore per unit.

Sustainability: 25% of eligible equipment costs (ETP, zero discharge, rainwater harvesting, e-waste and wastewater recycling, energy audits), excluding civil works, up to ₹25 lakh over the policy period.
conditions: Enterprise must be located in Kerala.
R&D support needs a collaboration with a university in Kerala.
Apply to the Department of Industries and Commerce or KSIDC.
apply: Kerala Department of Industries and Commerce / KSIDC

items.name: SME IPO listing support (Kerala Industrial Policy 2023)
items.summary: 50% of public-issue expenses on NSE/BSE SME platforms reimbursed, up to ₹1 crore
details: Reimbursement of 50% of expenses for a public issue on the NSE Emerge or BSE SME platform.
Maximum ₹1 crore.
conditions: MSMEs only.
Funds raised must be used to set up or expand an enterprise in Kerala.
Apply to the Department of Industries and Commerce or KSIDC after listing.
apply: Kerala Department of Industries and Commerce / KSIDC

items.name: Keravan Kerala caravan tourism investment subsidy (Kerala Caravan Tourism Policy)
items.summary: Investment subsidy for buying tourist caravans and camper vans; Rs 7.5 lakh per caravan paid to entrepreneurs so far
details: Kerala Tourism gives an investment subsidy and other incentives to private caravan operators and caravan park developers under Keravan Kerala.
By May 2024, 13 entrepreneurs had received Rs 7.5 lakh each (Rs 97.5 lakh in all).
In November 2025 camper vans were added as eligible vehicles for the subsidy.
conditions: Operator must enter an agreement with the Kerala Tourism Department before buying the caravan
Caravan must be registered with Kerala Tourism and meet the caravan policy norms
Apply to the Department of Tourism, Kerala

items.name: Theeramythri micro-enterprise programme for fisherwomen (Society for Assistance to Fisherwomen, SAF)
items.summary: Grant of 75% of project cost, up to ₹1 lakh per member (₹5 lakh for a 5-member group), for fisherwomen enterprises
details: Group enterprises of 2 to 5 women get a grant of 75% of project cost, up to ₹5 lakh on a project of about ₹6.67 lakh; bank loan covers 20% and members put in 5%.
Paid in two instalments: first for fixed assets after the bank loan is sanctioned, second as working capital.
Any income activity is allowed, for example fish vending kiosks, dry-fish units, catering, bakery and food processing, tailoring or services.
items.extraFor: Priority for widows of fishermen, disaster-affected families, persons with disabilities, transgender persons and trained women
conditions: Only women listed in the Fisheries Department's Fisherfolk Family Register; age limit 50, with priority for ages 20 to 40.
Contact the SAF office (Aluva) or district Matsyabhavan to apply.
items.onlyText: Only for women from registered fisherfolk families in Kerala

items.name: SAF Working Capital Revolving Fund for fisherwomen micro-enterprises
items.summary: Interest-free working capital of ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh per group (up to ₹1.5 lakh for stores and seafood kitchens)
details: Interest-free support for existing fisherwomen activity groups to expand business, repaid in 20 equal instalments.
Community provision stores, seafood kitchens and supermarkets can get up to ₹1.5 lakh.
conditions: For SAF-supported fisherwomen activity groups in Kerala.
Contact the SAF office to apply.
items.onlyText: Only for fisherwomen activity groups supported by SAF, Kerala

items.name: Kerala 'Government as Marketplace' procurement support for startups (KSUM)
items.summary: Government bodies can buy directly from startups up to Rs 20 lakh; EMD, experience and turnover exempted
details: Government departments can purchase directly from startups up to Rs 20 lakh.
A government order exempts startups from EMD, prior work experience and turnover criteria in tenders.
conditions: Startup registered with Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM).
Apply through KSUM's procurement facilitation or bid in state tenders.

items.name: Kerala Startup Policy (KSUM): innovation grant, seed fund and rent subsidy
items.summary: Innovation grant up to Rs 12 lakh, seed fund Rs 25 lakh to Rs 2 crore, rent subsidy up to 50%
details: Innovation grant up to Rs 12 lakh.
Seed Fund Scheme support of Rs 25 lakh to Rs 2 crore.
Scale-up rent subsidy of up to 50% of rent or Rs 20 per sq ft, whichever is lower, in government parks or leased premises.
items.extraFor: Seed Fund for Women Entrepreneurs has a two-year moratorium.
conditions: Startup registered with Kerala Startup Mission.
Apply on the KSUM portal during scheme calls.

states.statusText: In force.

portal.label: Industries and Commerce Department; apply at DIC Leh or Kargil

states.zones: Rates are the same across Leh and Kargil.
states.notes: Services qualify only if on the Annexure-II list, and trading is not covered. There is no interest subsidy, SGST refund or power concession.

items.name: DPR preparation subsidy
items.summary: 50% of project report (DPR) consultant cost, max ₹50,000, for projects of ₹25 lakh or more.
details: 50% of the consultant fee for the DPR, max ₹50,000. Project investment must be at least ₹25 lakh.
items.extraFor: Women who are single mothers or widows, persons with 40% or more disability, and third-gender persons: 95% of the DPR fee, max ₹1 lakh.
conditions: New units, or substantial expansion (at least 25% added plant and machinery investment)
Services only from the Annexure-II list

items.name: Stamp duty and registration fee reimbursement
items.summary: 100% reimbursement of stamp duty and registration fee on land in UT Industrial Estates, for new units.
details: 100% of stamp duty and registration fee on the conveyance or lease deed for land allotted in UT Industrial Estates. Paid after commercial production starts.
conditions: New units only
UT Industrial Estate land only

items.name: Transport subsidy (air freight)
items.summary: 50% of air freight on finished goods sent out of Ladakh, max ₹5 lakh a year for 5 years.
details: 50% of air freight on finished goods from Ladakh to any destination in India, max ₹5 lakh per unit per year for up to 5 years. Cannot be combined with the export incentive.
conditions: New and existing units
Claimed yearly

items.name: Green energy installation subsidy
items.summary: 50% of the cost of solar, wind or hybrid systems (10–2000 KW), max ₹25 lakh.
details: 50% of purchase and installation of solar, wind or hybrid systems of 10–2000 KW, max ₹25 lakh. Project investment must be at least ₹25 lakh. Paid 40%, 40% and 20% over 2 years. Existing units qualify only when replacing DG sets.
conditions: Project investment of at least ₹25 lakh

items.name: Wastewater recycling and pollution control assistance
items.summary: 50% of wastewater recycling tech (max ₹2 lakh); 50% of pollution control equipment for existing units (max ₹20 lakh).
details: Wastewater recycling: 50% of technology and machinery cost, max ₹2 lakh; new and existing units; civil works excluded. Pollution control devices: 50%, max ₹20 lakh; existing units only.
conditions: Paid after a satisfactory commissioning report

items.name: Quality certification and testing
items.summary: 35% of certification or testing equipment cost, max ₹5 lakh.
details: 35% of certification or testing-equipment cost after obtaining GMP, ISO, ISI, BIS, FPO, BEE, AGMARK, ECOMARK, ZED or GHP marks, max ₹5 lakh. Production machinery is excluded.
conditions: New and existing units

items.name: Trade fair and common facility centre support
items.summary: 50% of trade fair costs (max ₹2L, ₹1L, ₹50K for 1st–3rd fairs); 50% of CFC use.
details: Trade fairs and fashion shows: 50% of registration and space cost, max ₹2 lakh (1st), ₹1 lakh (2nd) or ₹50,000 (3rd). Common facility centre use: 50%, max ₹1 lakh a year for 3 years.
conditions: Handicraft, handloom, agro and food processing, or aromatic and medicinal plant units, cooperatives and FPOs only

items.name: Export incentive
items.summary: 60% of transport cost to an Indian export port, max ₹5 lakh a year for 5 years.
details: 60% of transport cost up to the international air or sea port in India, max ₹5 lakh a year for 5 years. Export sample shipping: up to ₹50,000 a year for 2 years.
conditions: Registered export units
Cannot be combined with the air-freight subsidy

items.name: Concessional industrial land (Land Allotment Policy 2025-35)
items.summary: 30-year leases at ₹0.75–6 lakh per kanal; 70% of estate land reserved for micro and small units.
details: Premium per kanal ranges from ₹1.0L urban / ₹0.75L rural (plots up to 3 kanal) to ₹6.0L / ₹5.5L (over 20 kanal). 70% of estate land is reserved for micro and small units; 40% for priority sectors, 10% for start-ups, 10% for underprivileged sections. Lease 30 years, extendable to 60.
items.extraFor: 10% of plots reserved for women who are single mothers or widows, persons with disabilities and third-gender entrepreneurs.
conditions: Order No. 115 I&C (UTL) of 2025 dated 21 Feb 2025; valid 10 years
Apply through the DIC with a DPR

items.name: Enterprising Ladakh Innovation and Startup Policy 2020
items.summary: Startup support with monthly allowance up to Rs 20,000, growth grant up to Rs 3 lakh, marketing aid up to Rs 3 lakh, patent and GST reimbursement up to Rs 5 lakh each
details: Run by the Directorate of Industries and Commerce, UT Ladakh; incubation centres in Leh and Kargil.
A revised Startup Policy Ladakh (staged support for ideation, seed and founder support, and J&K Bank interest subvention) was under review in August 2026.
conditions: Startup based in Ladakh; eligibility per the policy and the revised framework.
Apply through the Directorate of Industries and Commerce, Ladakh.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised under the Ladakh startup policy

items.name: Ladakh Homestay Policy 2023
items.summary: Startup kit worth up to Rs 1.25 lakh plus 75% of flush-toilet cost (up to Rs 1.25 lakh) for rural homestays
details: New homestays get a furnishing and solar equipment kit (up to Rs 1,25,000), Rs 50,000 for furnishings, and 75% of the cost of a winter-friendly flush toilet up to Rs 1,25,000.
Homestays set up under the 2020 policy can get 75% of toilet upgrade cost, up to Rs 1,00,000.
Best Homestay Awards of Rs 10,000 per sub-division.
items.extraFor: Preference to ex-servicemen, ex-Agniveers and households with no employed member
conditions: Ladakh resident with land in own name; homestay of 1 to 6 rooms outside Leh and Kargil municipal limits.
Mandatory training; must operate for at least 5 years after incentives or repay.
Apply to the Assistant Director (Tourism), Leh or Kargil, using the policy's application form; policy valid 5 years from notification.

states.statusText: The Department of Industries offers a 25% capital investment subsidy for new micro and small units. Applications follow an annual advertisement, so ask the Director of Industries whether a round is open.

portal.label: Lakshadweep Administration

source.label: DPIIT States' Startup Ecosystem Ranking: Lakshadweep report

states.notes: The ₹6.25 lakh cap and the conditions come from a summary of the scheme guidelines; confirm them with the department.

items.name: 25% Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme (Department of Industries, Lakshadweep)
items.summary: One-time subsidy of 25% of the cost of a new micro or small unit (land, machinery, building), up to ₹6.25 lakh.
details: 25% of the total project cost, including land, machinery and construction, capped at ₹6.25 lakh; paid once, in kind.
Investment in plant, machinery and building must be below ₹25 lakh.
Registered societies and self-help groups can also apply.
conditions: Residents of Lakshadweep aged 18 or over
New micro or small manufacturing or service units, not on the negative list
Not available if the same subsidy was received from LDC, LKVIB, the Coir Board, the Coconut Development Board or NABARD
Apply after the annual advertisement, to the DC/SDO of your island

states.statusText: In force through the MSME Promotion Scheme 2025. Figures below come from news reports; confirm them with the District Trade and Industries Centre.

portal.label: MP MSME Department

states.zones: Units in notified priority or backward blocks get extra help; the block list is in the scheme annexure.
states.notes: Sector packages exist for pharma and medical devices, food processing, apparel and textiles, footwear, furniture and toys.

items.name: Industrial development subsidy / investment promotion assistance
items.summary: Up to 40% of eligible investment (plant, machinery, building); 48% for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.
details: Reported: export-oriented units up to 52%; backward or priority-block units up to ₹1.3 crore; paid over 5–7 years; extra assistance linked to FDI and employment.
General caps and instalment rules unconfirmed.
items.extraFor: SC/ST and women: 48% instead of 40%
conditions: Expansion, diversification and technology upgradation treated the same as new units (official Invest MP summary)
Services/trading eligibility unconfirmed

items.name: Employment generation and skill assistance
items.summary: Medium units creating over 100 jobs: ₹5,000 per employee per month for up to 5 years.
details: Skill-training aid of ₹13,000 per trained worker (reported; size limits unconfirmed).
conditions: Reported at Cabinet approval; scheme conditions unconfirmed

items.name: Export and freight support (MSME scheme plus MP Export Promotion Scheme 2025)
items.summary: Freight aid to gateway ports and air cargo for exporting MSMEs (reported cap ₹2 crore), plus export-scheme grants.
details: MP Export Promotion Scheme 2025 (covers MSMEs): certification up to ₹10 lakh; trade fairs 75% up to ₹5 lakh a year; export infrastructure up to ₹1 crore; green certification up to ₹20 lakh a year.
conditions: Must be an exporting unit

items.name: Quality certification and IPR assistance
items.summary: Reimbursement for ISO, BIS, BEE, ISI, AGMARK and ZED certifications and patents; IPR support reported up to ₹10 lakh.
details: Organic/eco certification reported up to ₹5 lakh; the rate for each certificate is unconfirmed.

items.name: Environment (ETP) and last-mile infrastructure support
items.summary: 50% of ETP or eco-system cost up to ₹10 crore; last-mile infrastructure up to ₹5 crore (reported).
details: Whether this applies to single units or only clusters is unconfirmed.

items.name: Mukhyamantri Udyam Kranti Yojana (MMUKY)
items.summary: Loans ₹1-50 lakh (manufacturing) or ₹1-25 lakh (service/trade) with 3% interest subsidy and guarantee fee for 7 years
details: 3% a year interest subsidy on the outstanding loan for up to 7 years, including moratorium.
CGTMSE guarantee fee paid by the state for up to 7 years.
Loans were still being given in Jan 2026 (MP Startup Summit).
conditions: MP resident aged 18 to 40, at least 12th pass; family income up to ₹12 lakh a year.
New enterprise only; not a defaulter; no other self-employment scheme benefit.
Apply on the SAMAST portal.
items.onlyText: Only new entrepreneurs aged 18 to 40 with 12th pass

items.name: Sant Ravidas Swarojgar Yojana
items.summary: Loans ₹1-50 lakh (industry) or ₹1-25 lakh (service/trade) with 5% interest subsidy and guarantee fee for 7 years
details: 5% interest subsidy on the bank loan for 7 years.
Guarantee fee covered for 7 years.
conditions: Scheduled Caste applicants aged 18 to 45; 8th pass mark sheet needed.
