Claim through the financing bank and District Village Industries Officer
apply: Contact the District Village Industries Officer (UPKVIB)

items.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee Powerloom Weaver Electricity Flat Rate Scheme (Uttar Pradesh)
items.summary: Flat monthly power charge for powerlooms: Rs 400 (0.5 HP) or Rs 800 (1 HP) in cities, Rs 300 or Rs 600 in rural areas
details: Approved by the UP cabinet on 5 April 2023, effective 1 April 2023, outlay about Rs 400 crore.
Connections above 5 kW get a subsidy of Rs 700 per HP, up to Rs 9,100 a month, deducted from the bill.
conditions: Powerloom weaver with a powerloom electricity connection in Uttar Pradesh.
Apply through the Handloom and Textile Industry Directorate, UP, and the power distribution company.
items.onlyText: Only for powerloom weavers
apply: UP Handloom and Textile Industry Directorate

items.name: Mukhyamantri Hathkargha evam Powerloom Udyog Vikas Yojana (Uttar Pradesh)
items.summary: Subsidy for upgrading looms: up to 80% for handloom and up to 60% for powerloom equipment
details: Approved by the UP cabinet in April 2023 alongside the powerloom flat-rate scheme.
Covers upgrading traditional handlooms and powerlooms for all weavers of the state.
conditions: Handloom or powerloom weaver in Uttar Pradesh.
Apply through the district Assistant Commissioner, Handloom and Textiles.
items.onlyText: Only for handloom and powerloom weavers
apply: UP Handloom and Textile Industry Directorate

items.name: UP Tourism Policy 2022: capital or interest subsidy for tourism units
items.summary: 25% capital subsidy (up to Rs 2 crore) on Rs 10 lakh to Rs 10 crore investment, or 5% interest subsidy for 5 years
details: Capital subsidy on eligible capital investment: 25% up to Rs 2 crore for Rs 10 lakh to Rs 10 crore; 20% up to Rs 7.5 crore for investment up to Rs 50 crore.
Instead of capital subsidy, a unit can take 5% interest subsidy for 5 years on a bank loan up to Rs 5 crore (heritage hotels can take both).
Also: 100% stamp duty exemption on first transaction, 100% exemption on land conversion and development charges, 100% EPF employer-share reimbursement for 5 years.
Other support: 25% of ICT equipment cost, 75% of energy audit cost, 50% of green certification fees, 50% of event space rent for marketing (up to Rs 30,000 national / Rs 1 lakh international event).
items.extraFor: Extra 5% capital subsidy for women, SC/ST and backward-class entrepreneurs, Tier-2 and smaller towns and Focus Tourism Destinations
conditions: Covers hotels, resorts, heritage hotels, eco-tourism stays, wellness centres, theme parks and other notified tourism units
Total incentives capped at 30% of capital investment
Apply to UP Tourism Department / through Invest UP

items.name: UP IT and ITeS Policy 2022 (amended 2026): capital, interest and EPF support for IT units
items.summary: Capital subsidy (25% of FCI outside Noida/Ghaziabad after 2026 amendment, min Rs 2 crore), 7% interest subsidy for 5 years, EPF reimbursement
details: Base policy: 10% capital subsidy on fixed capital investment, 10% OPEX support (lease rent, bandwidth, cloud, power), 25% land cost reimbursement and 100% stamp duty exemption.
Interest subsidy of 7% a year for 5 years, up to Rs 1 crore a year; 100% EPF reimbursement up to Rs 1 crore a year; recruitment assistance of Rs 20,000 per employee.
Certification support up to Rs 25 lakh per unit, patent filing cost reimbursement and 50% course fee reimbursement (up to Rs 50,000 per candidate).

First amendment (2026): smaller IT firms outside Noida and Ghaziabad get 25% capital subsidy with minimum investment cut to Rs 2 crore; co-working space developers get 25% capex support up to Rs 20 crore.
conditions: For IT/ITeS units (software, BPO, IT services) set up or expanding in UP
Eligibility now also counts employment and business capacity, not only capital investment
Apply through Invest UP / Nivesh Mitra

items.name: UP Warehousing and Logistics Policy 2022: capital subsidy for warehouses, cold chain and logistics
items.summary: 15% capital subsidy for storage facilities (up to Rs 5 crore, Rs 10 crore in Logistics Zones) plus 10-year electricity duty exemption
details: Storage facilities (warehouse, silo, cold chain): 15% capital subsidy up to Rs 5 crore, or Rs 10 crore in designated Logistics Zones.
Logistics parks and dry ports: 25% up to Rs 25 crore; cargo terminals 20% up to Rs 15 crore; inland vessels 25% up to Rs 5 crore.
100% electricity duty exemption for 10 years, quality certification reimbursement up to Rs 5 lakh per storage project, and skill development subsidy.
Stamp duty exemption of 50% to 100% by region for storage facilities; 75% concession on land use conversion and development charges.
conditions: Minimum project size: warehouse Rs 20 crore and 1 lakh sq ft; cold chain Rs 15 crore and 20,000 sq ft; silos Rs 30 crore
Capital subsidy paid after commercial operations start
Apply through Invest UP / Nivesh Mitra

items.name: UP Dairy Development and Milk Products Promotion Policy 2022: capital and interest subsidy for dairy units
items.summary: 10% capital subsidy up to ₹5 crore plus 5% interest subvention for 5 years on loans for dairy and cattle-feed units
details: Capital subsidy of 10% of plant and machinery, technical civil works and spares, capped at ₹5 crore, for new milk processing or milk products units or expansions adding at least 25% capacity.

Interest reimbursement up to 5% a year for 5 years; caps include ₹10 crore (new milk processing unit), ₹7.5 crore (new cattle feed unit), ₹2.5 crore (technology upgrade or dairy expansion), ₹1 crore (cold chain such as bulk milk coolers and reefer vans) and ₹2 crore (micro and small units making value-added products like cheese and ice cream).
Stamp duty on land bought or leased for the unit is reimbursed; MSME units also get 50% of testing/standardisation fees (up to ₹5 lakh) and up to 75% of patent/design fees (up to ₹5 lakh).
conditions: Policy notified 17 Oct 2022 for five years (to about Oct 2027).
Open to private entrepreneurs, FPOs, milk producer companies and co-operatives; incentives start after commercial production.
Apply online through the Dairy Development Department portal linked to Nivesh Mitra.

items.name: UP Poultry Development Policy 2022: interest subsidy for layer and broiler parent farms
items.summary: 7% interest reimbursed for 5 years on bank loans for commercial layer and broiler parent farms, plus duty exemptions
details: Project funded with 30% margin money and up to 70% bank loan; 7% a year of interest on the loan is reimbursed for 5 years.
100% electricity duty rebate for 10 years for poultry units set up under the policy.
100% stamp duty exemption on land bought or leased for the unit.
conditions: Covers commercial layer farms and broiler parent farms set up under the policy.
Apply through the UP Animal Husbandry Department (nodal agency) portal.

items.name: Uttar Pradesh public procurement relaxations for startups (UP Startup Policy 2020)
items.summary: Startups exempt from prior experience, turnover and EMD conditions in state tenders and on GeM
details: Startups are exempted from prior experience, turnover and EMD requirements on GeM bids of state buyers.
Departments such as Energy, Home, Medical Health and Planning have issued tenders with turnover and experience relaxations for startups.
State agencies are encouraged to allocate a share of procurement to startups.
items.extraFor: Preference for startups owned by women, Divyangjan and transgender entrepreneurs.
conditions: DPIIT-recognised startup registered with Startup in UP.
Claim the relaxation in the bid; check each tender for the startup clause.

states.statusText: In force. Figures come from press reports of the 2023 notification; confirm the rates with the DIC.

portal.label: Invest Uttarakhand single window

states.zones: Categories A and B are hill areas (higher rates); C and D are mostly plains.
states.notes: Covers manufacturing only; service businesses fall under the Service Sector Policy 2024.

items.name: Capital subsidy (MSME Policy 2023)
items.summary: Capital subsidy capped by category: micro ₹50 lakh (A) to ₹20 lakh (D); medium up to ₹4 crore.
details: Maximum subsidy. Micro (investment up to ₹1 cr): A ₹50L, B ₹40L, C ₹30L, D ₹20L. Small: A ₹1.6 cr, B ₹1.2 cr, C ₹80L, D ₹60L. Medium (₹10–50 cr): A ₹4 cr, B ₹3 cr, C ₹2 cr, D ₹1.5 cr. Percentage rates unconfirmed. Paid in 2 yearly instalments (up to ₹1 cr) or 5 instalments (₹1–50 cr).
items.extraFor: +5% for units owned by women, SC, ST or persons with disabilities. One report gives caps of ₹5L micro, ₹10L small, ₹15L medium; another gives ₹10/15/20L. +5–10% for priority and ultra-priority manufacturing.
conditions: Manufacturing only; the service sector is excluded from this policy
Whether expansion qualifies is unconfirmed (false used as the conservative value)
Subsidy percentages and the 'small' investment slab are unconfirmed

items.name: Stamp duty reimbursement
items.summary: Stamp duty reimbursed 100% in categories A and B, 75% in C, 50% in D for new units.
details: New MSME units get back stamp duty paid: 100% (A, B), 75% (C), 50% (D). Which documents are covered (land or building purchase or lease) is unconfirmed.
conditions: New manufacturing units
Rate set by the unit's location category

items.name: Interest subsidy on loans
items.summary: Interest subsidy exists and was raised from the 2015 policy; rates, caps and duration unconfirmed.
details: Rates, annual caps and duration by category are not confirmed; ask the DIC.
conditions: Terms unconfirmed

items.name: Mandi fee exemption for hill agro-processing units
items.summary: 50% mandi fee exemption for 5 years for agriculture-based processing units set up in hill areas.
details: 50% exemption from mandi (market) fee each year for 5 years for new agro-based processing units in hill areas.
conditions: Agro or food-processing activity
Unit in a hill area (which categories count is unconfirmed)

items.name: Quality certification, trademark and patent assistance
items.summary: Up to ₹1 lakh for national or international quality certification, quality marking, trademark or patent.
details: Up to ₹1 lakh for quality certificates, quality marking, trademarks and patents. Press also reports ZED medal rewards of ₹75,000 (Gold), ₹50,000 (Silver) and ₹25,000 (Bronze); unconfirmed.
conditions: Whether existing units qualify is unconfirmed

items.name: Mukhyamantri Swarozgar Yojana 2.0 (MSY 2.0)
items.summary: Margin money subsidy 15-30% (plus 5% booster) on projects up to ₹25 lakh (manufacturing) or ₹10 lakh (service/trade)
details: Zones A and B: 30% up to ₹2 lakh, 25% for ₹2-10 lakh, 20% for ₹10-25 lakh. Zones C and D: 25%, 20% and 15%.
One extra 5% booster for rural/Nagar Panchayat location, women or divyang applicants, or ODOP/GI manufacturing.
Own contribution 10% (5% for special categories); bank finances the rest.
Runs FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30; subsidy adjusted to the loan after two years of operation.
items.extraFor: Own contribution 5% for SC, ST, OBC, minority, ex-servicemen, women and divyang; extra 5% subsidy for women and divyang
conditions: Uttarakhand permanent/native resident aged 18+; no education bar.
Not a defaulter; one beneficiary per family; no other self-employment scheme in the last 5 years.
Apply online; DIC scrutiny and district committee selection, then bank sanction.
apply: District Industries Centre / MSY online portal

items.name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023 incentives
items.summary: Seed fund up to ₹10 lakh (₹12.5 lakh priority groups) and monthly allowance ₹15,000 (₹20,000 priority groups) for 12 months
details: Seed fund of up to ₹10 lakh; up to ₹12.5 lakh for priority groups, plus ₹2.5 lakh extra for disruptive technology.
Monthly allowance of ₹15,000 for recognised startups, ₹20,000 for priority groups, for up to 12 months.
100% patent cost reimbursement up to ₹1 lakh (Indian) and ₹5 lakh (international).
At least 15% of seats in state-supported incubators reserved for women-led startups.
items.extraFor: Women, SC/ST, divyang and transgender founders (and rural-impact or disruptive-tech startups) get ₹20,000 a month and up to ₹12.5 lakh seed fund
conditions: Startup recognised under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023 (Startup Uttarakhand).
Apply on the Startup Uttarakhand portal.
items.onlyText: Only for startups recognised under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy

items.name: Mukhyamantri Ekal Mahila Swarozgar Yojana (single women self-employment)
items.summary: 75% grant on self-employment projects up to ₹2 lakh for single women; beneficiary puts in 25%
details: Project support of up to ₹2 lakh, of which 75% is a state grant and 25% the beneficiary's share.
Grant paid by DBT in instalments; first phase launched 10 Feb 2026 (₹3.45 crore to 484 women), second phase launched July 2026.
Run by the Women Empowerment and Child Development Department, Uttarakhand.
conditions: Single women resident in Uttarakhand: unmarried, widowed, divorced, abandoned or destitute women, acid-attack survivors, women affected by crime, and transgender persons.
Business must be set up near the applicant's home or in the local area.
Apply through the district Women Empowerment and Child Development office.
items.onlyText: Only for single, widowed, divorced, abandoned or destitute women and transgender persons in Uttarakhand
apply: Women Empowerment and Child Development Department, Uttarakhand (district office)

items.name: Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Paryatan Swarozgar Yojana (tourism self-employment)
items.summary: 33% subsidy up to ₹33 lakh in hills (25% up to ₹25 lakh in plains) for tourism businesses
details: Covers hotels/paying guest, fast food, yoga centres, adventure, tented stays, handicraft shops, caravans, floating hotels and similar tourism units.
Vehicles (bus, taxi, electric bus): 25% up to ₹10 lakh; selected pushback, AC or electric buses 50% up to ₹20 lakh.
Applicant puts in 12.5% of project cost as margin money; rest is a bank loan.
conditions: Permanent residents of Uttarakhand
Tourism-related activity (NIC 49, 55, 56, 79, 93)
Apply online on the MSY portal through the District Tourism Officer
items.onlyText: Only for permanent residents of Uttarakhand

items.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Griha Awas (Homestay) Vikas Yojana
items.summary: Homestay subsidy 33% up to ₹10 lakh (hills) or 25% up to ₹7.5 lakh (plains), plus 50% interest subsidy for 5 years
details: Interest subsidy of 50% for the first five years of repayment, up to ₹1.5 lakh a year in hills and ₹1 lakh a year in plains.
conditions: Homestay units registered with Uttarakhand Tourism (NIC 5510)
Apply through the District Tourism Development Officer

items.name: Assistance Scheme for Handloom Spinning-Weaving Women Workers (Uttarakhand)
items.summary: 90% subsidy up to Rs 25,000 on looms and handloom tools; beneficiary pays 10%
details: Covers looms and related spinning and weaving equipment.
conditions: Traditional women workers whose main occupation is handloom weaving or spinning in Uttarakhand.
Apply through the district industries centre / handloom office.
items.onlyText: Only for women handloom spinners and weavers

items.name: Uttarakhand procurement benefits for startups (Startup Policy 2023)
items.summary: Direct purchase from recognised startups up to Rs 10 lakh (excl. GST) and exemptions under the Purchase Preference Policy
details: State agencies can buy directly from recognised startups up to Rs 10 lakh (exclusive of GST).
Recognised startups get exemptions under the Uttarakhand Purchase Preference Policy in state tenders and RFPs.
conditions: Startup recognised under the Uttarakhand Startup Policy 2023.
Register on the Startup Uttarakhand portal and claim exemptions in the bid.

states.statusText: In effect from 1 Oct 2026 for new manufacturing units and approved expansions (approved 20 Jul 2026). The earlier Banglashree scheme closed on 31 Mar 2025.

portal.label: MSME and Textiles Department (single window: silpasathi.wb.gov.in)

states.zones: Rates vary across Zones A, B and C; the district list comes with the notification.
states.notes: Covers manufacturing only; services and trading are not covered. Figures come from launch reports because the gazette text is not yet available.

items.name: Interest subsidy on term loan
items.summary: 25% (Zone A) or 35% (Zones B, C) of annual term-loan interest for five years.
details: Zone A: 25% of annual interest liability; Zones B and C: 35%; for 5 years from first loan disbursement. Annual or total cap unconfirmed.
conditions: New unit starting commercial production on or after 2026-10-01
Udyam registration required
Units that started production on or before 2026-09-30 are ineligible

items.name: Electricity duty waiver
items.summary: Electricity duty waiver for five years: 50% in Zone A, 75% in Zones B and C.
details: Zone A: 50%; Zones B/C: 75%; five years from commercial production. Micro/small units wholly owned by women or SC/ST: 100% waiver for five years, max ₹10 lakh a year.
items.extraFor: Micro/small units wholly owned by women or SC/ST: 100% waiver, max ₹10 lakh/year
conditions: New units from 2026-10-01; also listed for approved expansion of existing MSMEs
Medium coverage inferred from 'MSMEs' wording - confirm

items.name: Quality certification reimbursement
items.summary: 50% of ISI/BIS/ISO/HACCP certification cost; cap ₹5 lakh micro/small, ₹10 lakh medium.
details: Reimbursement of 50% of certification costs (ISI, BIS, ISO, HACCP); ceiling ₹5 lakh for micro and small, ₹10 lakh for medium enterprises.
conditions: WBIS 2026 unit (production from 2026-10-01)
Eligibility of expansion units unconfirmed

items.name: Expansion support package (capital subsidy, stamp duty/registration fee reimbursement, power subsidy)
items.summary: Approved expansions of existing MSMEs get capital subsidy, stamp-duty/registration reimbursement, power subsidy and duty waiver.
details: Components reported only; rates, caps and zone differentials unconfirmed.
conditions: Existing Udyam-registered manufacturing MSME
Expansion must be approved under WBIS 2026

items.name: MSME cluster infrastructure support
items.summary: Cluster infrastructure subsidy up to ₹5 crore per eligible MSME cluster.
details: Cluster must have at least 5 MSMEs, ₹250 crore combined investment and 500+ workers; total subsidy capped at ₹5 crore per cluster.
conditions: Cluster-level application, not an individual-unit benefit
items.onlyText: For MSME clusters applying together, not a single unit

items.name: West Bengal Bhabishyat Credit Card Scheme (WBBCCS)
items.summary: Collateral-free loan for projects up to ₹5 lakh, 10% margin money grant (max ₹25,000), interest of only 4% for youth
details: Project cost up to ₹5 lakh as term loan, working capital or composite loan; state pays 10% of project cost as one-time margin money, capped at ₹25,000.
No collateral or third-party guarantee; up to 100% guarantee (CGTMSE up to 85% plus state up to 15%).
Interest subsidy scheme from 1 Apr 2024: borrower pays 4% a year, state covers up to 8.5% a year while the account stays standard.
conditions: West Bengal resident for at least 10 years, aged 18 to 45, one person per family, not a bank defaulter or government employee.
New or existing income-generating micro units in manufacturing, services, trading or farm-allied activities.
Apply online; block or sub-division committees screen and sponsor applications to banks.
items.onlyText: Only for West Bengal residents aged 18 to 45

items.name: West Bengal Textile Incentive Scheme 2022 (WBTIS 2022)
items.summary: 10–20% capital subsidy on plant and machinery by textile activity, power subsidy ₹1–2/unit for 5 years, stamp duty refund
details: Capital investment subsidy: e.g. weaving/knitting 20% (max ₹10 crore), dyeing and processing 20% (max ₹20 crore), technical textiles 20% (max ₹25 crore), circular knitting 10% (max ₹5 crore).
100% electricity duty waiver for 5 years; power subsidy ₹1 to ₹2 per unit for 5 years (garments ₹1/unit, cap ₹50 lakh a year).
100% stamp duty and registration fee reimbursement; land conversion and mutation fee waiver; 25% of ETP cost up to ₹1.5 crore; energy audit and conservation support.
Expansion needs at least 25% rise in plant and machinery and in turnover. MSMEs choose between WBTIS and other state schemes.
items.extraFor: Primary handloom weavers' co-operatives get 6% working-capital interest subsidy, extra marketing incentive and 10% export assistance
conditions: Textile, apparel or technical textile manufacturer with Udyam registration; commercial production on or after 1 Apr 2022
Apply online to the Directorate of Textiles within 12 months of starting production
Powerloom sub-scheme closed (last date 30 Dec 2025)
items.onlyText: Only for textile, apparel and technical textile manufacturing units

items.name: WBMDFC self-employment term loan and margin money (minorities)
items.summary: Term loans up to ₹5 lakh at 5–6% a year; margin money up to 25% of project cost (max ₹1.25 lakh) at 4%
details: West Bengal Minorities Development & Finance Corporation term loan: 5% a year up to ₹50,000, 6% above; repayable in 20 quarterly instalments over 5 years; guarantor needed.
Margin money scheme for projects up to ₹5 lakh: bank finances 60%, WBMDFC up to 25% (max ₹1.25 lakh) at 4%.
Covers small business, trade, cottage industry, services, artisans and transport.
conditions: Member of a notified minority (Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, Parsee) within the corporation's family-income limits; not a loan defaulter
Apply in the prescribed form at the BDO/Panchayat Samity (rural), SDO office (municipal) or GM, DIC Kolkata
items.onlyText: Only for members of notified minority communities in West Bengal

items.name: West Bengal Food Processing Incentive Scheme 2021 (WBFPIS)
items.summary: 40% credit-linked capital subsidy on plant and machinery, up to ₹10 lakh per micro food unit
details: Back-ended grant released in two equal instalments linked to loan use and start of production.
Can be combined with Banglashree incentives, electricity duty and stamp duty waivers, but not with another capital subsidy on the same machinery.
Scheme period was 2021-22 to 2025-26 (ended 31 March 2026); check with the department whether a new scheme is open.
conditions: Micro food processing units (NIC 10), including individuals, SHGs, NGOs and co-operatives; rice mills, aerated and packaged water excluded
Not in Kolkata, Howrah, Siliguri, Asansol, Durgapur, Bidhannagar or Chandannagar municipal corporation areas
Bank term loan is mandatory; apply to Department of Food Processing Industries and Horticulture
apply: WB Food Processing Industries and Horticulture Dept

items.name: Preference to West Bengal MSEs in state purchases (WBFR Rule 47A, Finance Dept order 6142-F(Y), 2017)
items.summary: State-based registered MSEs get preference in WB government tenders if they match the lowest valid price
details: Finance Department order No. 6142-F(Y) of 10 Oct 2017 modified Rule 47A(1) of the West Bengal Financial Rules.
Preferences earlier given to state SSI units now apply to West Bengal-based registered micro and small enterprises.
The preference is for selection only: the MSE must agree to supply or execute at the lowest valid bid price, otherwise the order goes to the L1 bidder.
conditions: Micro or small enterprise based in West Bengal and registered under the MSMED Act (Udyam).
Claim the preference in the bid and accept the L1 price.

items.name: Assistance to Individual Handloom Weavers (West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024)
items.summary: One-time Rs 5,000 for work-shed or loom repair plus Rs 10,000 for yarn bought through Tantuja
details: Part of the West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024 (MSME and Textiles Department).
conditions: Individual handloom weavers not covered by a primary weavers' co-operative society; weaver registration and SSY card needed.
Apply online or offline in the prescribed form; district and state committees approve.
items.onlyText: Only for individual handloom weavers outside co-operatives

items.name: West Bengal Homestay Tourism Policy: one-time grant for registered homestays
items.summary: Rs 1 lakh grant per registered homestay (two instalments of Rs 50,000) to upgrade rooms and facilities
details: Rs 50,000 after registration on submitting an approved expenditure plan to the District Magistrate's office, and Rs 50,000 after work is done (invoices within 6 months).
Can be spent on sanitation, kitchen hygiene, basic furniture, soft furnishings, minor room changes, and optionally TV and WiFi.
Other benefits: electricity and water at domestic rates, residential property tax rates and exemption from land conversion charges.
Figures are from the 2022 policy; the state issued a new West Bengal Homestay Policy 2026 with Gold and Silver categories, so check the current amounts.
conditions: Owner or family member must live in the same property
1 to 6 rooms (up to 12 beds), each with attached toilet
Register at wbhomestaytourism.gov.in or with the District Magistrate's office (fee Rs 1,000 Gold, Rs 500 Silver)
